title: Placebo instructions in an exactly solved harness: does the ceiling rise through what the block says or that it is there
statement: In the card paper's released MiniWoB++ sandbox (github.com/2020-qqtcg/HRP; three task families, 576 test tasks, one token per action, soft-Bellman optimum), add three instruction blocks to H0 that match H5's length and format: a wrong-content block (the other family's procedure), a content-free block (generic diligence and format rules with no procedure) and an inverted block (H5's procedures with their order and conditions reversed), three rewordings each. For every arm recompute, exactly, the frozen base model's reference distribution $\pi^{\mathrm{ref}}(\cdot\mid s)$ at every reachable state, the KL-regularised ceiling $C$ by the paper's soft Bellman solve, the frozen base model's and the released H0-trained checkpoint's mismatch $M$ and success. The readout is the ceiling-gain ratio $\rho_{\mathrm{arm}} = \Delta C_{\mathrm{arm}} / \Delta C_{H5}$, with $\Delta C_{\mathrm{arm}} = C(\mathrm{arm}) - C(H0)$ and $\Delta C_{H5} = 0.081$ for H0 to H5 (Table 10), beside the reference's log-probability shift on the H0-optimal action, $\Delta\ell_{\mathrm{arm}} = \mathbb{E}_{s \sim d^{*}_{H0}}[\log \pi^{\mathrm{ref}}_{\mathrm{arm}}(a^{*}(s)\mid s) - \log \pi^{\mathrm{ref}}_{H0}(a^{*}(s)\mid s)]$, where $a^{*}(s)$ is the H0-optimal action and $d^{*}_{H0}$ the H0 optimum's discounted state occupancy.
claim: In an exactly solved harness, a same-length instruction block with the wrong content raises the harness's ceiling by at least half of what the right instructions raise it, because the ceiling moves through the base model's prior mass on well-formed actions, not through the procedure the block describes.
trick: Give the agent the right instructions, the wrong instructions and empty-calorie instructions of the same length, and compute exactly, not by sampling, how much of the harness's best achievable return each one adds.
why_now: The card paper (v2, 2026-10-28) released a sandbox in which the ceiling is computed exactly by dynamic programming and reports that H5, which 'only adds instructions', raises the ceiling by 0.081 through the reference policy it induces (Table 10; sec. 5.3); content was never varied. CL-W43-10's deployment probes (C-W43-07, C-W43-20) measure a placebo's effect on sampled yield, where ceiling and mismatch cannot be separated; this is the first setting where the placebo's effect on what the harness offers is a certified number. The identity itself is the old regularised-MDP performance-difference lemma; the enabling piece is the released solver and the H5 text, and that is the flag.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 ($0, 1 day): clone HRP, confirm the soft Bellman solver, the compiled graphs for the 576 test tasks, the H0 and H5 system messages and the H0-trained Qwen3.5-2B checkpoint are released (if the solver is missing, stop and park: the exact readout is the point). Step 1 (1 day): write three rewordings each of three blocks matched to H5's token length within 5%: wrong-content (the checkbox families receive the ascending-numbers procedure and the number family receives the checkbox procedure, with 'deciding when to submit' rewritten for the wrong family's termination rule), content-free (diligence and format rules only), inverted (H5's procedures with the order and conditions reversed, a negative control that must lower the ceiling if content matters). Step 2 (about 20 GPU-hours on one RTX 4090 or A100): for each of 1 + 1 + 9 encodings (H0, H5, nine placebo texts) run the frozen Qwen3.5-2B at every reachable state of every test task with thinking disabled, logits normalised over the single-token menu (the paper's protocol, App. F.1), solve the regularised optimum per task family and compute $C$, the frozen base's $M$ and success, and the released H0 checkpoint's $M$ and success under each encoding; report per family and family-weighted, with the spread over the three rewordings as the error bar. Readouts: $\rho_{\mathrm{arm}}$ for the three arms; $\Delta\ell_{\mathrm{arm}}$; the frozen base's and H0 checkpoint's success change per arm.
killing_experiment.kills_if: On all three families, the wrong-content and content-free blocks give $\rho_{\mathrm{arm}} < 0.25$ across all three rewordings, and the inverted block gives $\rho < 0$: the ceiling moves through what the instructions say. Then presence has no footing in the one setting where what the harness offers is a certified number, CL-W43-10's deployment probes inherit a content reading as their prior, and the result is the first exact positive control for content effects in harness design (citable either way).

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment probability 0.45: the content-free block recovers $\rho \ge 0.5$ on at least two of three families and the wrong-content block does too, with $\Delta\ell$ showing the reference's gain concentrated on the submit and terminal decisions and on valid-code mass, while the inverted block gives $\rho$ near zero rather than strongly negative; the frozen base's success moves with the ceiling in every arm.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: The card paper, sec. 5.3: 'Three of the seven switch to H5, which only adds instructions, so a revision that changes no action can still raise the ceiling through the reference it induces'; Table 4 defines H5 by its content, 'additional system instructions for matching labels, tracking tile IDs, correcting selections, and deciding when to submit'; App. F.1: 'Because H5 changes the reference model's input as well as the actor's, we solve its regularized optimum separately from H0's even though their execution dynamics coincide.' The ceiling gain is read as what those instructions induce; whether their content is what induces it is not asked.
preregistered_surprise.would_change: If presence wins: the ceiling term of the card's identity, for prompt-only harness revisions, is a format-compliance term, so 'raises the ceiling' is not 'teaches the procedure'; harness-search methods that score prompt revisions by a fixed model's return (the card's intro: Hu et al. 2025, Zhang et al. 2025b, Fernando et al. 2023) are selecting for form, and CL-W43-10 gains an exact mechanism. If content wins: the first exact number on a content effect in harness design; CL-W43-10's deployment placebos get a calibrated prior and the claim's 'presence' reading must come from a search-policy change (tool-call counts), which C-W43-07 and C-W43-20 measure.

scorecard.target_value: In print: the card paper reads the H5 ceiling gain as induced by the instructions' content (sec. 5.3, Table 4) and leads its abstract with harnesses being 'judged by how an already trained model performs under them'; CL-W43-10's current belief quotes harness papers attributing per-model context effects to the information in the block. Who pays: harness-search and prompt-optimisation builders (the card's intro cites four), every scaffold paper that adds a system-instruction block and reports the gain as design, and the two deployment placebo probes of CL-W43-10, which need to know what a content effect looks like where it can be certified.

impact_ceiling.floor: A short note on the released sandbox: the placebo ceiling-gain ratio per family with its rewording spread, cited by the next harness-geometry or prompt-sensitivity paper. Requires steps 0 to 2. Judgment p 0.5.
impact_ceiling.middle: The mechanism of CL-W43-10 in one solvable setting (the reference's valid-action mass, not the procedure, carries a prompt-only ceiling gain), adopted as the placebo arm that harness-search papers run before claiming a prompt revision raised what the harness offers. Requires the presence outcome plus the same computation on the paper's H1 to H4 with a placebo instruction block appended. Judgment p 0.3.
impact_ceiling.ceiling: A rule for prompt-only harness revisions, confirmed at deployment scale by C-W43-07 and C-W43-20: a same-length placebo recovers a stated fraction of every instruction block's gain, so harness leaderboards add a placebo column. Requires both deployment probes to agree with the exact result. Judgment p 0.1.

scorecard.relevance: Narasimhan (tau-family, scaffold sensitivity): direct, the certified form-versus-content split is the lane's attribution question. HAL (Narayanan): moderate, harness columns re-read. Evaluators and harness-search builders: direct. Industry: moderate (what to spend on in a system prompt). Jacob's edge: dynamic programming on finite graphs, a KL-regularised Bellman solve and an exact identity are his register; theoretical physics zero beyond the identity; GPU engineering small (one 2B model, batched forward passes).
scorecard.kill_probe: Steps 0 to 2 (about 24 GPU-hours, about $30 cloud or $0 on a local GPU, 5 days); dead if the wrong-content and content-free blocks give $\rho < 0.25$ on all three families across all rewordings and the inverted block gives $\rho < 0$.
scorecard.density_and_ownership: From the card's fetched neighbours: FormatSpread 2310.11324 measures accuracy spread over meaning-preserving formats on frozen models (up to 76 points) with no control problem and no ceiling; Harness-Zero 2609.24974 and the co-evolving-harness paper 2609.09134 train under harnesses and never vary instruction content against a placebo; WHALE 2609.00196 searches harnesses by a fixed model's return. Occupied by the card: the identity, the H5 ceiling gain of 0.081 and the sandbox. Not occupied: any placebo or content-free instruction arm, any decomposition of a prompt-only ceiling gain. The kill search must use the neighbours' words (prompt sensitivity, instruction ablation, irrelevant instructions, system prompt, format robustness, KL-regularised reference, harness revision, prompt optimisation) and quote the limitation text of 2310.11324 and 2609.00196; density is counted on the day of writing. Ownership: the card's authors (HKUST Guangzhou) hold the solver and can run this in a day; the re-open test is asking whether they have varied H5's content.
scorecard.why_now: Card paper v2 2026-10-28 with code; the sandbox makes the placebo's effect on the ceiling exact. The identity is old; the flag is recorded.
scorecard.register_and_not: Measurement (an exact control arm on a released solvable sandbox) with a mechanism (the reference's prior) and a recipe consequence (a placebo arm for prompt-only harness revisions). It is not a new harness, not a prompt-optimisation method, not a deployment-scale result, and not a claim about tools or executors, which the placebo leaves untouched.

identifiability: Random given: nothing in the readout is sampled. $C$ is a property of (encoding, frozen base model Qwen3.5-2B, $\tau = 0.1$, $\gamma = 0.95$, the compiled graphs) computed by dynamic programming; $M$ and success for a checkpoint are exact under the paper's single-token menu protocol with thinking disabled at temperature 1, so the quantities are properties of the encoding and the model, not of a sampling protocol. The one free choice is the block text, so each arm carries three rewordings and the spread is the error bar; length is matched in tokens of the base model's tokenizer within 5%. The instruction block changes the reference and the actor's input and nothing else (H5's own construction: 'execution dynamics coincide'), so $\Delta C$ is attributable to $\pi^{\mathrm{ref}}$ by construction. The H0 checkpoint's success under a block is a readout-drift number (card asymmetry 2), reported but secondary.
positioning_note: Lab-adjacent: a released sandbox, one consumer GPU, no artifact needed; solo covers the whole probe. The card's authors can run it in a day; asking them is the re-open test. Dropped operators: operator 4 (a ruler grading published prompt-only harness revisions by their placebo ratio) is the middle scenario, not a separate probe; operator 1 (replace the teacher-as-optimum in the coding study with the same model at higher effort) is C-W43-11's effort-notch control in different clothes and is not re-proposed; a frozen-model readout-drift probe under the paper's R1 to R5 presentation variants (unreported, card asymmetry 2) is a floor-effect risk for the 2B base and is left to the kill search as a cheap addition if the 9B's H0 success in App. F.8 is high enough to lose.
neighbors_to_check_first: 2610.37255 App. F.1 and Table 4 — the H5 system message text and length; whether the HRP release includes the soft Bellman solver, the compiled test graphs and the H0-trained checkpoint
2310.11324 — FormatSpread: whether any instruction-content ablation (not format) is run, and its limitation text
2609.00196 — WHALE: whether Meta-Harness search scores prompt revisions with any placebo or length control
2609.09134 — co-evolving harnesses: whether the evolved harness's instruction content is ablated against a same-length block
C-W43-07 and C-W43-20 (this repo) — the deployment placebo arms of CL-W43-10, so the three probes share one definition of the placebo ratio
headline_test: Instruction blocks raise what a harness offers through the base model's prior on well-formed actions: a same-length block with the wrong content raises an exactly computed harness ceiling by at least half as much as the right one.
claim_attachment_note: the mechanism probe of CL-W43-10 in the one setting where what the harness offers (ceiling) and how the model reads it (mismatch) are separable and exact; C-W43-07 and C-W43-20 are the deployment-scale yield probes; detach to orphan only if the claims stage reads CL-W43-10 as about pasted retrieval context alone and not system instructions

title: Five coding harnesses at matched thinking tokens: is the fixed-model harness ranking an effort ranking
statement: Rerun the card paper's five coding harnesses (DeepAgents, Pi coding-agent, DeepSeek Harness, Terminus-2, mini-SWE-agent) with the same frozen Qwen3.5-9B on Terminal-Bench Lite (39 tasks) under a server-enforced cap on thinking tokens per model call, $B_d \in \{512, 2048, 8192, \infty\}$, three runs per cell, logging thinking tokens, output tokens and model calls per task, and read each harness's accuracy against its realised total generated tokens per task as a score-versus-spend curve. Zero-dollar step from the paper's Tables 2 and 13: the mean model calls per complete trajectory (Terminus-2 4.9, Pi 6.6, mini-SWE-agent 8.6, DeepSeek Harness 8.6, DeepAgents 14.2) correlate with accuracy at Spearman $-0.67$ by our computation (mid-ranks for the tie), against $-0.7$ for the paper's mismatch $\widetilde{M}_h$, while the per-call mismatch $\widetilde{M}_h / \bar{L}_h$ ($\bar{L}_h$ the mean calls per trajectory) correlates at $-0.1$, so the paper's own fit term orders the harnesses by how many calls the model makes. Readouts: the between-harness accuracy spread at matched realised tokens on the common support of the five curves, as a fraction of the default-budget spread (64.1% to 47.9%, Table 2), each with its three-run standard error; and the share of harness accuracy variance over the 20 cells explained by realised tokens and calls per task.
claim: At a fixed open model, the ranking of coding harnesses on Terminal-Bench Lite is a ranking of thinking tokens and model calls per task: at matched realised spend the five harnesses' accuracies fall within their run-to-run spread of each other.
trick: Give every scaffold the same thinking budget per task and see whether the scaffolds still differ, or whether the ones that looked better were the ones that made the model think more.
why_now: The card paper (v2, 2026-10-28) is the first fixed-model five-harness comparison with recorded model calls per trajectory and an estimator whose fit term 'grows with the number of decisions a harness asks of the model' (sec. 6.3), yet it reports no token counts and varies no budget: Qwen3.5-9B runs with thinking on, temperature 0.6 and a 32,768-token output limit (App. F.7). CL-W43-03's attached probes (C-W43-11, C-W43-18) are API runs on ARC-AGI-3 costing $1,600 to $2,200, which the claim's Gate 1 note flags as borderline; an open model on a local GPU gives the effort clause a probe under one GPU-week with no API dollars. The thinking-token cap is standard serving machinery (close the thinking segment at the cap); nothing else is new, and that is the flag.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 ($0, 1 day): from the HRP release, check whether per-trajectory token counts for the 585 Terminal-Bench Lite runs (5 harnesses x 39 tasks x 3 runs) are logged; if so, compute Spearman between mean generated tokens per task and accuracy across the five harnesses and the within-harness tokens-versus-success relation across tasks, before any new run. Step 1 (about 80 GPU-hours on two H100s, 7 days): serve Qwen3.5-9B with vLLM, thinking on, temperature 0.6, the paper's 32,768 output and 65,536 context limits and 50-decision cap; enforce the per-call thinking cap $B_d$ by stopping the thinking segment at $B_d$ tokens and appending the close tag (the $\infty$ arm reproduces the paper); run 5 harnesses x 39 tasks x 4 caps x 3 runs = 2,340 trajectories in the Terminal-Bench Lite containers, logging thinking tokens, output tokens, model calls and wall time per task. Compute per harness the accuracy-versus-realised-tokens curve with three-run standard errors; on the common support of realised tokens, the between-harness spread at matched tokens by linear interpolation; and a two-way fit of cell accuracy on log realised tokens and log calls per task with harness as a residual factor. Both outcomes are reported with the ordering at each cap.
killing_experiment.kills_if: At matched realised tokens on the common support, the five harnesses keep the default ordering and a between-harness spread of at least 75% of the default spread, beyond two three-run standard errors for at least three of the four adjacent pairs: harness design carries accuracy that effort cannot buy on this stack, and the effort clause of CL-W43-03 is refuted for coding harnesses with an open model (the ARC-AGI-3 API arm C-W43-11 stands on its own).

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment probability 0.5: the spread at matched realised tokens falls below half of the default spread, the residual ordering follows calls per trajectory (fewer calls, higher accuracy at equal tokens), and the $B_d = 512$ arm compresses all five harnesses to within their run-to-run spread; so what survives of 'harness design' at a fixed model is how many times the harness makes the model stop and restart its reasoning, not its tools or prompts.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: The card paper's abstract: 'For coding-agent harnesses on Terminal-Bench Lite, ceiling minus mismatch estimated with a stronger model as a stand-in for the optimum reproduces the accuracy ranking, while either term alone does not'; sec. 6.3: 'With the model fixed, the harness moves Terminal-Bench Lite accuracy from 47.9% to 64.1%. We ask whether the ceiling and the mismatch explain this ordering.' The ordering is read as what each harness offers minus how well the model uses it; spend is not a variable (App. F.7 fixes thinking on, temperature 0.6 and a 32,768-token output limit).
preregistered_surprise.would_change: If effort explains it: fixed-model harness leaderboards (Terminal-Bench's agent table, HAL's harness columns) report accuracy at matched generated tokens, the card's mismatch term is re-read as a call-count term for coding agents, and CL-W43-03 gains a GPU-only probe that passed. If design survives: the first matched-spend evidence that coding harness design has value beyond effort at a fixed open model, with the matched-token spread as its size; the next question is which harness component (tool set, prompt, control loop) carries it, by swapping components at matched spend.

scorecard.target_value: In print: the card paper reports a 16.2-point fixed-model harness spread with no token column and a fit term that grows with model calls (sec. 6.3, Table 13); CL-W43-03's current belief quotes 2610.22289 sec. 9.3 ('Further analysis is needed to determine their relative contributions') and HAL's finding that higher effort can lower scores. Who pays: harness builders (the five harness teams) whose rankings are quoted at a fixed model, leaderboard owners (Terminal-Bench, HAL) ranking harnesses, and any team choosing a scaffold for an open model on a token budget.

impact_ceiling.floor: A matched-spend table for five public harnesses on one open model, with score-versus-spend curves and the call-count correlation, cited by the next harness comparison. Requires step 1. Judgment p 0.5.
impact_ceiling.middle: The effort clause of CL-W43-03 established on a second stack (open model, coding harnesses, GPU only) beside the ARC-AGI-3 API arm, so scaffold papers report accuracy at matched generated tokens as a rule. Requires the effort outcome and one more model (a 27B to 35B open model, about 150 GPU-hours more). Judgment p 0.3.
impact_ceiling.ceiling: A leaderboard rule: harness columns carry a matched-spend accuracy and a calls-per-task column, adopted by Terminal-Bench or HAL; the card's ceiling-minus-mismatch ranking is re-read as a call-count ranking in print. Requires adoption by one leaderboard owner. Judgment p 0.1.

scorecard.relevance: HAL (Narayanan): direct, cost-controlled harness comparison. Narasimhan (tau-family): direct, scaffold sensitivity and effort. Evaluators and harness builders: direct. Industry: direct for scaffold choice on open models. Jacob's edge: serving a 9B model with a token-cap hook and running five harnesses against sandboxed containers is computer engineering; the matched-spend curves and the variance fit are evaluable; theoretical physics zero.
scorecard.kill_probe: Step 0 ($0, 1 day) then step 1 (about 80 GPU-hours, $0 API, 7 days); dead if the harness ordering and at least 75% of the default spread survive at matched realised tokens beyond two three-run standard errors.
scorecard.density_and_ownership: From the card's neighbours and this repo's records: HarnessBandit 2609.13739 and WHALE 2609.00196 treat harnesses as training choices and report no matched-spend comparison; 2512.08296 (C-W43-06's record) gives a capability-saturation rule for scaffold effects without matching tokens; HAL 2510.11977 reports effort effects from single runs (CL-W43-14); C-W43-11 matches normalized tokens on ARC-AGI-3 through the vendor's effort notch and a restart controller, with API dollars. Occupied by the card: the five-harness accuracy table, the decisions-per-trajectory counts and the teacher-based estimates. Not occupied: any token or budget arm, any matched-spend harness comparison with an open model. The kill search must use the neighbours' words (thinking budget, reasoning budget, test-time compute, agent scaffold, harness comparison, turn limit, max steps, cost-controlled evaluation) and quote the limitation text of 2610.22289 and 2607.12227 (CL-W43-03 gate 6); density is counted on the day of writing. Ownership: the harness teams and Terminal-Bench's maintainers hold the runs; the card's authors hold the 585 trajectories, and step 0 asks whether they logged tokens.
scorecard.why_now: Card paper v2 2026-10-28 with recorded calls per trajectory and no budget arm; Qwen3.5-9B and all five harnesses are open; the thinking cap is standard serving machinery. The flag that nothing else is new is recorded.
scorecard.register_and_not: Measurement (a matched-spend comparison the paper did not run) with a recipe consequence (report harness accuracy at matched generated tokens; count calls). It is not a new harness, not the card's estimator on a new benchmark, not an ARC-AGI-3 replication, and not a claim about restarts, which this stack cannot vary cleanly within a Terminal-Bench container.

identifiability: Random given: the task container at a pinned Terminal-Bench Lite version (deterministic after the action up to tool timing), one served model at the paper's temperature 0.6 with thinking on, one harness configuration per arm, and the cap $B_d$; run-to-run variance is the policy's sampling plus serving nondeterminism, which three runs per cell measure. Realised tokens per task is the matched quantity and is a property of (harness, model, cap), so matching is done on the realised value, not the cap, by interpolation on the common support; a harness whose curve never reaches another's support is reported as unmatched, not extrapolated. Success is the benchmark's own test verifier, not a judge. The 512-token arm changes the model's behaviour inside a call (truncated reasoning), so the curve is read as spend-at-cap, not as a free-running model stopped early; the paper's 32,768 limit is the $\infty$ arm.
positioning_note: Solo: open model, open harnesses, local GPUs, $0 API, no artifact; lab-adjacent to HAL as a consumer. Dropped operators: operator 1 (replace the teacher-as-optimum with the same model at maximum thinking budget) collapses into this probe's $\infty$ arm and C-W43-11's effort notch; operator 4 (a per-decision mismatch map from the paper's recorded per-state student and teacher samples, card asymmetry 3) is a credit question for L2 and reads as a footnote on three tasks; a restart arm is not proposed because a Terminal-Bench container cannot be resumed from a fresh context without changing the task state.
neighbors_to_check_first: 2610.37255 App. F.7 and the HRP release — whether per-trajectory token counts and model-call logs for the 585 runs are included; the five harnesses' configurations and the 50-decision cap
2610.22289 — C-W43-11's paper: its sec. 9.3 limitation text and whether any token-matched harness comparison exists there
2512.08296 — the capability-saturation rule for scaffold effects: whether tokens or calls are matched
2510.11977 — HAL: the effort-versus-accuracy cells and whether any harness comparison is cost-matched
C-W43-11 and C-W43-18 (this repo) — the ARC-AGI-3 effort-clause probes, so the three share one definition of matched spend
headline_test: At a fixed open model, coding-harness rankings are rankings of thinking tokens and model calls: at matched spend the five harnesses tie.
claim_attachment_note: the effort clause of CL-W43-03 on a second stack (open model, coding harnesses, GPU only, under one GPU-week), answering the claim's Gate 1 dollar note; C-W43-11 and C-W43-18 are the ARC-AGI-3 API arms; it does not test the restart clause

title: Second draw for the harness grid: within-cell run and judge spread against the harness rankings TraceTrial-Bench reports
statement: Re-run a stratified slice of the released 4-harness x 9-model x 95-task grid with replicates: 4 harnesses x 2 models (the model with the largest single-run harness swing at the lowest Table 7 cost per run, and one open-weight model served locally through the paper's own loopback LiteLLM gateway) x 30 tasks stratified over the seven dimensions x 5 runs, same Docker images, judge and archived reasoning settings, and re-judge every stored trace three times so the spread splits into a run component and a judge component. Step 0 before any run (zero dollars): count the replaced cells per harness and model and, where the archive retains the replaced first execution, compute the within-cell flip rate on Agent pass and the change in $p_H/n_H$ (passed over finalized harness criteria, eq. 3) between the first and the replacement draw, the only within-cell pair that exists today, biased toward cells that failed first, which is the selection rule's own size. Readouts: per cell the run-to-run standard deviation of Agent pass and of $p_H/n_H$; variance components per model, $\sigma^2_h$ (harness), $\sigma^2_{h \times t}$ (harness-by-task), $\sigma^2_{\mathrm{run}}$ (replicate residual net of judge) and $\sigma^2_{\mathrm{judge}}$ (re-judging the same trace); the fraction of run-bootstrap resamples in which each model's 4-harness ordering on task success and on harness macro is unchanged; and the smallest harness difference the grid resolves at its own size, $\Delta_{\min} = 1.96\sqrt{2(\hat\sigma^2_{\mathrm{run}} + \hat\sigma^2_{h \times t})/95}$, set beside the reported 12.2-point macro range (59.8% to 72.0%) and the 22.1 and 23.2-point task-success swings (Grok-4.6: 33.7% OpenClaw to 55.8% Claude Code; Opus 5: 30.5% Codex to 53.7% Claude Code; Table 7, sec. 5.3).
claim: At fixed model, a second run of the same harness-task cells reorders the four harnesses, and the resolvable difference it measures, $\Delta_{\min}$, exceeds the adjacent-harness gaps in at least 5 of the 9 archived model groups: the per-model harness rankings a harness benchmark reports are draws, resolved only at the extremes, and part of the spread is the judge.
trick: Run the same harness on the same task again, and count how often the ranking of harnesses changes before anyone argues about why one harness is better.
why_now: The card paper (2026-10-23) released the grid with traces, verdicts, Docker images and a loopback gateway, so four native harnesses can be re-run without re-engineering four adapters, and it states in print that it 'does not estimate within-cell repeatability' (sec. 4.1). 2607.17136 (2026-07-19) supplies the prior from agentic RL: run-to-run nondeterminism is a dominant variance component on the hardest cell, the run distribution is bimodal, and 'a single-run improvement of the size this field publishes would have the wrong sign roughly one-third of the time', with a k-seed reporting library released. Harness-Bench 2605.27922 (2026-05) is the second harness benchmark whose abstract states no runs per cell, so two harness leaderboards now exist with zero within-cell numbers. The estimator (variance components, bootstrap over runs) is old; the flag is recorded.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 (zero dollars, 2 days): from the release, the count of replaced cells per harness and model group; where the replaced first execution is retained, the within-cell Agent-pass flip rate and the paired change in $p_H/n_H$, reported with the selection caveat (replaced cells are those that failed first). Step 1 (API dollars plus local serving, 7 days): 4 harnesses x 2 models x 30 tasks x 5 runs = 1,200 runs. Model A: of the two headline-swing models (Grok-4.6, Opus 5), the one with the lower Table 7 cost per run; model B: an open-weight model from the paper's nine served on 2 H100s through the gateway, or Qwen3.8-27B as the substitute, logged as a deviation. Tasks: 30 drawn to the seven dimensions' proportions (15:27:9:19:7:17:1), fixed before the run. Everything else as archived: harness versions (Appendix B.1), Docker images, task revisions, resolved reasoning settings, judge deepseek-v4-flash at the archived budget per cell. Re-judge each of the 1,200 traces three times at the archived budget (about 3,600 judge calls). Fit per model the crossed random-effects decomposition of Agent pass and of $p_H/n_H$ into $\sigma^2_h$, $\sigma^2_t$, $\sigma^2_{h \times t}$, $\sigma^2_{\mathrm{run}}$ and $\sigma^2_{\mathrm{judge}}$; bootstrap over runs within cell to get the ordering-stability fraction for the 4-harness ranking and the 95% band on each pairwise harness gap; compute $\Delta_{\min}$ at 95 and at 30 tasks. Report the single-run archived ordering for the same cells beside the 5-run ordering.
killing_experiment.kills_if: Step 1, both models: the within-cell flip rate on Agent pass is under 10%, each model's 4-harness ordering on task success is unchanged in at least 95% of run-bootstrap resamples, and $\hat\sigma^2_{\mathrm{judge}}$ is under one tenth of $\hat\sigma^2_{\mathrm{run}}$. Then the cells are near-deterministic, the single-run grid resolves its own rankings, and CL-W43-14's 'spread larger than the differences' is false for harness identity; the result is the first within-cell repeatability number for a harness benchmark and confines the lane's replicate rule to cost and effort, citable either way.

title: Is the harness effect at fixed model an effort and restart effect? Dose-matched re-analysis of the released grid, then a pinned-effort rerun through the gateway
statement: Step 0 (zero dollars): from the release's per-run token_usage events (reasoning tokens, output tokens) and lifecycle events (compactions, fresh sessions, subagent spawns), fit per model group $m$ the logistic model $\mathrm{logit}\,P(\mathrm{pass}_{h,m,t}) = \alpha_m + \beta_h + \gamma \log D_{h,m,t} + \delta N_{h,m,t} + u_t$, with $h$ the harness, $t$ the task, $D$ the run's reasoning-token dose, $N$ its count of context resets and $u_t$ a task random effect, and report how much the harness contrasts $\beta_h$ shrink when $\gamma$ and $\delta$ enter, in particular the share $1 - \Delta^{\mathrm{adj}}/\Delta^{\mathrm{raw}}$ of the Claude Code vs Codex gap on Opus 5 ($\Delta^{\mathrm{raw}} = 23.2$ points, Table 7) predicted away at the pooled median dose and zero resets. Step 1: because Claude Code and Codex both route through one loopback LiteLLM gateway (Appendix B.1), rewrite every request there to pin the same reasoning setting on both harnesses for one model, and in a second arm cut both at the same cumulative output-token budget $B$; 2 harnesses x 95 tasks x 2 arms x 2 runs = 760 runs, Agent pass and the per-dimension harness-criterion profile as readouts. The matched quantity is reasoning tokens (and total output tokens under the cut), which the paper logs per run and never matches ('Reasoning settings follow the archived configurations', sec. 4.1).
claim: The harness effect at fixed model that harness benchmarks report is in large part the harnesses' default reasoning settings and restart counts: pinned to one effort and one token budget at the gateway, the Claude Code vs Codex gap on Opus 5 falls to under half of its single-run 23.2 points.
trick: Make both harnesses ask the model to think the same amount, cut both off at the same spend, and see how much of the harness advantage is left.
why_now: The card paper (2026-10-23) is the first public grid where reasoning tokens, context resets and harness identity are all logged per run at fixed model and task, and it states the unmatched settings as its own limitation: 'Variation in task revisions, runtime settings, and scoring budgets further constrains causal conclusions about individual harness design choices' (sec. 6.1). Its gateway topology (two native harnesses through one loopback LiteLLM endpoint) is the enabling piece for the pinned-effort arm: one request rewrite applies to both harnesses without touching either. CL-W43-03's existing probes (C-W43-11, C-W43-12, C-W43-18) test self-written scaffolds on ARC-AGI-3 games at 1,000 dollars to 2,200 dollars; this is the cross-vendor harness instance with a zero dollars step 0.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 (zero dollars, 3 days): extract per run $D$ (reasoning tokens; output tokens as the secondary dose), $N$ (compaction events, fresh-session relaunches and subagent spawns, pooled and separately), and the archived reasoning setting from the resolved configuration (Appendix C.3); fit the logistic model with and without $\gamma$ and $\delta$ per model group (380 runs each) and pooled with a model random effect; report the shrinkage of each harness contrast, the Opus 5 Claude Code vs Codex share, and the same for Grok-4.6 (22.1 points); report the gap within restart-count bins. Step 1 (API dollars, 7 days): Opus 5 as the headline model (Table 7 cost per run 0.660 dollars on Claude Code, 2.121 dollars on Codex), Grok-4.6 as the fallback if the Opus 5 cost of 760 runs exceeds 1,200 dollars. Arm P: the gateway rewrites the thinking or reasoning-effort field of every request to one value for both harnesses. Arm C: arm P plus a cumulative output-token cut $B$ equal to the archived median per-run output tokens of the cheaper harness on this model; the gateway refuses requests past $B$ and the deliverable is graded as it stands. 2 harnesses x 95 tasks x 2 arms x 2 runs = 760 runs, archived Docker images, task revisions and judge; the archived single-run cells are the baseline, with C-W44-41's run band as the noise reference where it exists. Readouts: the Claude Code vs Codex gap on Agent pass in arms P and C with a run-bootstrap band; the per-dimension harness-criterion profile (seven components) in each arm, which says which component carries whatever gap remains.
killing_experiment.kills_if: Step 0: entering $\log D$ and $N$ shrinks the Claude Code vs Codex contrast by under 25% in at least 7 of 9 model groups; and step 1: at pinned effort (arm P) and at the matched cut (arm C) the Claude Code vs Codex gap on the chosen model stays above half of its single-run value (above 11.6 of 23.2 points on Opus 5) and outside the run band. Then effort and restarts are not the gap; harness design carries it; CL-W43-03 is refuted on its cleanest public instance, and the per-dimension profile says which of the seven components carries it, citable either way.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment probability 0.5: in step 0 the dose and reset terms take between 35% and 65% of the per-model harness contrasts, and in step 1 the Opus 5 gap at pinned effort falls below 12 points, with the matched cut closing it further; the remainder sits in the Execution and Tools dimensions of the harness-criterion profile.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: The card paper attributes the harness swings to the harness ('how harness design interacts with model behavior', abstract) and names the confound only as a limitation: 'Reasoning settings follow the archived configurations' (sec. 4.1) and 'Task-specific revisions and recovery runs also limit causal interpretations of a difference between Harnesses' (sec. 4.2). Harness-Bench (2605.27922) concludes 'agent capability should be reported at the model-harness configuration level', reading the pairing as the unit. Neither matches reasoning tokens across harnesses.
preregistered_surprise.would_change: If effort and restarts explain the gap: harness benchmarks pin the reasoning setting at the gateway and report at matched budget, a leaderboard's harness column is read as an effort column, and vendor claims of one harness over another at fixed model are re-stated at matched effort. If they do not: harness design holds value independent of effort, and the per-dimension profile is the first decomposition of a cross-vendor harness effect into named components, with the next probe allocating by component (operator 3, the harness obligation as the unit).

identifiability: Step 0 is a mediation decomposition on observational runs where the dose $D$ and the reset count $N$ are caused by the harness; it bounds the share and does not identify the harness effect at fixed effort, which step 1 identifies by intervention: the gateway rewrite is the same object for both harnesses, applied to every request, visible to neither harness. Random given: the harness versions, model endpoint, task revisions, Docker image, judge and budget as archived; the pinned setting value; the cut $B$ counted at the gateway in the provider's output-token units. Restart count is observed, not pinned: a harness that resets context more by design keeps that as design, and the gap is reported within reset-count bins. Only the two gateway-routed harnesses are reachable (OpenClaw and DeepSeek Harness use native interfaces, Appendix B.1), which is the stated scope. Codex and Claude Code also differ in system prompt and tool set; those are harness design under the claim's own definition and are not matched. The reasoning setting the archive used per cell is read from the resolved configuration and reported beside each contrast, since unmatched settings are the paper's stated limitation and not ours.
positioning_note: Lab-adjacent: a zero dollars re-analysis of a released grid and an API-dollar intervention on two public harnesses; no frontier lab owns the cross-vendor question, and each vendor has an interest in one answer. Solo covers both steps. The paper's authors hold the gateway and can run arm P in a day; the re-open test is asking whether the resolved reasoning settings per cell are in the release. Dropped operators: 3 (allocate by harness component) waits on this result; 1 (replace the judge) is a service; 7 (effort as a sampler decision) is C-W43-11's design and is not duplicated.

scorecard.target_value: In print: the card paper's sec. 6.1 and 4.2 name unmatched runtime settings and recovery runs as the limit on causal conclusions about harness design; HAL (2510.11977, per the CL-W43-14 thread) reports higher effort giving equal or lower accuracy in 21 of 36 combinations; 2610.22289 sec. 9.3 (per the CL-W43-03 thread) says 'Further analysis is needed to determine their relative contributions'. Who pays: harness benchmark owners, harness vendors comparing products at fixed model, leaderboards with a harness column, and teams choosing a harness for a model on the strength of a 20-point single-run swing.

impact_ceiling.middle: The first pinned-effort, matched-budget cross-vendor harness comparison, with the share of the harness gap that is effort and the per-dimension profile of the remainder; a harness benchmark adopts gateway-pinned effort. Requires step 1. Judgment p 0.3.

title: Wrong fact at the boundary: is a harness-delivered block trusted over a tool call?
statement: On the Context-dimension tasks where the harness's delivery decides the outcome, intervene at the loopback gateway that Claude Code and Codex already route through, three arms per cell: the cross-turn fact or subagent return as delivered, a same-length wrong fact in the same format taken from another task, and the fact removed; 2 harnesses x 2 models x the qualifying tasks x 4 runs, measuring Agent pass, pre-answer verification tool calls (reads and commands whose result would re-acquire the fact, counted programmatically from tool_result events) and whether the wrong fact reaches the deliverable. Step 0 (zero dollars) decides which tasks qualify: from the released traces, split the 15 Context tasks' runs and the 144 subagent-aggregation runs (sec. 5.4) by the harness verdict and by whether a later tool_result re-acquired the fact, and compare Agent pass across delivered, dropped-and-reacquired and dropped-and-not-reacquired runs, which also reads the mechanism behind 48.4% harness satisfaction with 95.8% agent success on cross-turn retention and 46.2% vs 72.2% on subagent aggregation (sec. 5.4). The readout for the claim is the verification-call ratio $\rho = (c_{\mathrm{removed}} - c_{\mathrm{wrong}})/(c_{\mathrm{removed}} - c_{\mathrm{right}})$, with $c_{a}$ the mean pre-answer verification calls in arm $a$: $\rho \approx 1$ means presence suppresses checking whatever the content.
claim: Harness-delivered context carries authority: an agent verifies a fact the harness hands it at a turn boundary less than it searches for one the harness dropped, whatever the fact says, and carries a wrong one into the deliverable.
trick: Hand the agent a wrong fact through the same channel the harness uses for right ones, and count whether it checks it as often as it goes looking when nothing was delivered.
why_now: The card paper (2026-10-23) released the first per-run record of 'what the model could observe' at each boundary (model_input and tool_result events, sec. 2.3, 3.1) beside a harness verdict on whether the fact survived, and its sec. 5.4 numbers are the first saying the agent succeeds without the delivered content in about half the runs; its gateway topology lets the delivered content be rewritten without touching the harness, which is what a placebo arm on a native harness needs. CL-W43-10's probes (C-W43-07, C-W43-20) vary a scaffold block pasted in the prompt; this is the harness-channel instance, and CL-W43-05 (unsourced persistence in compaction summaries) is the L4 neighbour claim: a compaction summary is a harness-delivered block.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 (zero dollars, 2 days): for each Context task and the subagent-aggregation runs, from the release: the harness verdict on the retention or aggregation criterion, a programmatic check of whether any later tool_result contains the fact's source (file path or command output defined per task before reading any trace), and Agent pass; the three-group pass rates per task with Wilson intervals. A task qualifies when dropped-and-not-reacquired runs pass at least 20 points below delivered runs. Step 1 (API dollars, 4 days): on the qualifying tasks, 2 harnesses (Claude Code, Codex) x 2 models (Opus 5 and the cheapest Table 7 model among the nine) x 3 arms x 4 runs; the gateway rewrites the model_input of the boundary turn only: arm R as delivered; arm W a wrong fact of the same token length and format from another task of the same dimension; arm 0 the fact removed. Readouts per cell: Agent pass, pre-answer verification calls $c_a$, the fraction of arm-W runs whose deliverable contains the wrong fact, and $\rho$ with a run-bootstrap band. Expected size: 8 qualifying tasks, 384 runs, about 210 dollars in agent cost plus judge.
killing_experiment.kills_if: Either: step 0 finds no qualifying task (on every Context task, dropped-and-not-reacquired runs pass within 20 points of delivered runs, so the Agent criteria never need the fact; the intervention has nothing to move and the finding is a rubric-validity footnote on the paper, not a probe of CL-W43-10); or step 1 finds, in both harnesses, $\rho$ under 0.3 with a band excluding 0.7 and the wrong fact in under 20% of deliverables, so agents check what the harness hands them as hard as they search for what it dropped: the harness channel carries no authority and CL-W43-10 loses its harness-channel instance, with the measured verification rate as the citable number.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment probability 0.5: at least 5 of the 15 Context tasks qualify; on them $\rho$ is above 0.7 in both harnesses (the wrong fact suppresses verification calls as much as the right one, both at least 40% below the removed arm), and the wrong fact reaches the deliverable in over half of arm-W runs.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: The card paper grades the harness on delivering what the model could observe and reads the sec. 5.4 gap (48.4% harness satisfaction against 95.8% agent success on cross-turn retention) as harness unreliability the agent survives; its abstract: '31.1% of runs achieve task success despite failing at least one harness criterion'. The CL-W43-10 thread records the field's content reading of context effects (harness papers attribute a block's effect to the information in it). Nobody has varied the content of a harness-delivered block on a native harness.
preregistered_surprise.would_change: If the channel carries authority: harness builders attach provenance to delivered blocks and compaction summaries, harness benchmarks grade delivered-content correctness rather than presence, and CL-W43-10's placebo arm becomes the standard control for harness context (and CL-W43-05's unsourced persistence gets its inference-side cousin). If agents check regardless: the agent's own verification is the reliability mechanism, context-delivery fidelity is a cost item and not a correctness item, and the Context dimension of harness benchmarks is re-weighted accordingly.

identifiability: Random given: the same pinned harness versions, endpoints, task revisions, images, judge and reasoning settings as C-W44-41; the arms differ in exactly one block of the boundary turn's model_input, rewritten at the gateway and invisible to the harness, with token length matched in the provider's tokenizer as counted at the gateway. A verification call is defined per task before any trace is read (a tool call whose result contains the fact's source) and counted from tool_result events, a programmatic count with no judge; Agent pass uses the paper's criteria and judge, and the Harness-layer coupling (state 2 inherits the Agent verdict, Table 4) does not enter because the harness sheet is not a readout. The 45 fixed multi-turn tasks have scripted turns, so the boundary is the same event in every arm; simulator-driven tasks (4) are excluded. Only the two gateway-routed harnesses are reachable (Appendix B.1), the stated scope. The quantity $\rho$ is a property of (harness, model, task, block format); the format is held to the harness's own delivery format in all arms, so 'authority' is the channel's, not a formatting trick's.
positioning_note: Lab-adjacent: a zero dollars trace re-analysis and a 250 dollars intervention on public harnesses; L1 with an L4 crossover (compaction summaries and subagent returns are harness-delivered blocks). Solo covers both steps. The paper's authors can run step 0 from their archive in an afternoon; the re-open test is whether model_input events for the boundary turns are in the release. Dropped operators: 4 (grade harness benchmarks by whether delivery changes outcome) is step 0 alone and a footnote; 5 (a content-matched comparison across harnesses) is folded into the two-harness design.

title: Paired on nothing: instance share versus rollout share in EnvOS's generated-instance cells
statement: Re-run the two certified claims blocks of EnvOS (10 frozen instances, seeds 0-9, arms OFF-A and ON-A, 40-action budget) with $k = 5$ rollouts per cell for Claude Sonnet 5 through the Claude CLI and Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview through REST at the paper's pinned settings, one launch window per model, the paper's own validity classifier, scorer and reserve rule unchanged, and the optional Opus 5 clinic block (16 instances, OFF-A and LIVE-A) as step 2. Readouts per cell: the per-instance success rate $\hat p_{ic} = k^{-1}\sum_r Y_{icr}$ (instance $i$, arm $c$, rollout $r$, outcome $Y \in \{0,1\}$ from the committed row), the law-of-total-variance split $\mathrm{Var}[Y_{\cdot c}] = \mathrm{Var}_i[p_{ic}] + \mathbb{E}_i[p_{ic}(1-p_{ic})]$ with the instance share $\rho_I(c) = \mathrm{Var}_i[p_{ic}] / \mathrm{Var}[Y_{\cdot c}]$ estimated by the beta-binomial moment estimator with a bootstrap band, the replicate agreement of the sign test's discordant-pair set (which instances count as 'rescued' in rollout 1 against rollout 2, Cohen's $\kappa$), and the replicate-pooled paired estimate $\hat\Delta_k = n^{-1}\sum_i(\hat p_{i1} - \hat p_{i0})$ with its interval beside the paper's single-draw $8/0/2$ and $5/0/5$. Randomness named: the policy's token sampling (Gemini at temperature 1.0, top-$p$ 0.95, top-$k$ 64; the Claude CLI's unrecorded default, App. R) and the serving stack's nondeterminism; nothing from the environment, because the trigger fires on the first eligible request after the old value is served under a once-only guard, the grader re-derives the verdict from the committed row, and a misfired change, undelivered frame or provider failure voids the run before outcome (sec. 2.3, 7.1), so an episode's result is a function of the agent's own action sequence alone.
claim: In agent benchmarks whose instances are seeds of one generator, the instance explains none of the outcome variance: the paired-by-instance sign test is paired on nothing, the 'rescued instances' it counts are coin flips of the rollout, and the replicate that matters is the run.
trick: Run every cell five times instead of once and ask whether the same instances pass each time (the instance decides) or different ones (the dice decide); if the dice decide, pairing by instance bought nothing and the count of rescued instances is a count of coin flips.
why_now: EnvOS (2610.40246, v1 2026-10-29, v2 2026-11-02) is the first pre-registered paired A/B on computer-use agents whose validity classifier drives the environment, delivery and grader causes of a single failure to audited zero per episode, so a replicate matrix on its cells has exactly one leftover source of spread, the agent's own sampling plus serving; its supplement ships the environment, harness, invoker, scorer and certifier sources and the journaled digests of every request (Reproducibility statement; sec. CLM-BG 'All 626 task requests are journaled with the digests of their frame and text'), so the re-run is API calls on a released testbed. The pipeline's CL-W43-14 was nominated as the L1 champion on 2026-10-30 and has no probe on a short-horizon certified benchmark; this is its sharpest testbed because the effects are large and the non-agent buckets are zero by construction.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 (zero dollars, 2 days): obtain the OpenReview supplement (forum 9gw03JpKK4), rebuild the 14-service testbed with the shipped sources, run the shipped reproduction target to confirm Table 6 recomputes, run the scripted reference policy through the certifier to confirm the two claims task modules still certify, and record models.get for Gemini and the CLI version for Claude. Step 1 (the kill probe, 5 days): Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview and Claude Sonnet 5, claims block, 10 instances x {OFF-A, ON-A} x 4 new rollouts each (the paper's rollout is replicate 1), 160 rollouts of at most 40 actions, one launch window per model, validity classified before outcome by the shipped classifier, voided attempts logged with their reason and replaced under the shipped reserve rule, frames hashed so that any wall-clock drift in rendered pages is detected. Compute per cell $\hat p_{ic}$, $\rho_I(c)$ with a 1,000-resample bootstrap over instances and rollouts, $\kappa$ between the discordant-pair sets of any two rollouts (all 10 pairs of rollouts, reported as mean and range), and $\hat\Delta_5$ with the paired interval from the instance-level bootstrap. Step 2 (optional, 6 days, about $600): Opus 5 clinic block, 16 instances x {OFF-A, LIVE-A} x 4 new rollouts, same readouts, to see whether the $0/16 \to 15/16$ contrast is instance-deterministic.
killing_experiment.kills_if: In the Gemini ON-A cell (the paper's 5/10) and the Sonnet ON-A cell (9/10), at least 8 of 10 instances come out $\hat p_{ic} \in \{0, 1\}$ (all five rollouts agree), the bootstrap lower bound of $\rho_I(\mathrm{ON\text{-}A})$ exceeds 0.5 for Gemini, and the discordant-pair sets of different rollouts agree with mean $\kappa \ge 0.6$: the instance is the unit, the pairing is justified, the single rollout was an adequate reading of the policy on this protocol, and CL-W43-14 is confined to the cost and effort tables where the heavy-tailed per-run cost lives; the paper's design is then the first certified counterexample to the claim and is cited as such.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment probability 0.55: in the Gemini ON-A cell the ten instances are not bimodal, at least 5 of 10 sit at $\hat p_{ic} \in [0.2, 0.8]$, the bootstrap band of $\rho_I(\mathrm{ON\text{-}A})$ includes 0, and the rollout-to-rollout $\kappa$ of the rescued-instance set is below 0.3, so the 5/0/5 was five coin flips; the Sonnet cells are closer to instance-deterministic at the ends ($\hat p$ near 0 for OFF-A on most instances, near 1 for ON-A) with 2 to 3 instances in the middle, so the 8/0/2 reproduces as a pooled $\hat\Delta_5$ near $+0.7$ but the identity of the two tied instances changes from rollout to rollout.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: The paper: 'Inference is conditional on the fixed instances and one sampled policy rollout per condition' (sec. 7.3) and its primary test is 'an exact two-sided sign test on the discordant pairs' with instances as the pairing unit (sec. 7.3); the design treats the instance as the source of heterogeneity that pairing removes, and reports 'of the pairs, 7 rescues, 0 harms, 3 ties' (claims block) as counts of instances. Leaderboards more widely treat a single rollout per task as a reading of the policy (HAL 2510.11977: 'we were forced to rely on single runs without statistical validation for most evaluations', quoted in CL-W43-14).
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: If the instance share is near zero on seeded instances, then for generated-instance agent benchmarks (the CUA-Gym, STT-Arena and EnvOS pattern, where instances are seeds of a template) the instance is not a stratum, pairing by instance is cosmetic, the right design is rollouts per template with a binomial interval, and every per-instance reading ('13 of 16 rescued', 'found by exactly one model') is retired; the consequence for CL-W43-14 is that the run is the unit even where effects are large. If the instance share is high, the seeded instances carry real heterogeneity that a one-rollout paired design captures, and the claim's scope shrinks to cost and effort measurands.

title: Temperature zero in a certified-static world: the serving stack's share of agent outcome flips
statement: Use EnvOS's certification and validity-first counting as the control arm for the serving stack: run Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview on the released claims block (10 instances x {OFF-A, ON-A}, 40-action budget) at temperature 0 with $k = 5$ rollouts per cell, in the same launch window as the sibling temperature-1.0 matrix, with the paper's REST invoker, inline frames and journaled per-request digests of frame and text unchanged. Readouts: the first-divergence step $d_{icr} = \min\{t : (\text{input digest at } t \text{ equal across rollouts}) \wedge (\text{action at } t \text{ differs})\}$ per rollout pair, the fraction of rollout pairs action-identical through the commit, the per-cell outcome flip count $F_{ic} = \min(\sum_r Y_{icr},\ k - \sum_r Y_{icr})$, and the within-cell variance at $T = 0$, $\mathbb{E}_i[\hat p_{ic}(1-\hat p_{ic})]$, as a floor under the $T = 1.0$ within-cell variance from the sibling matrix, so that the within-cell spread splits into a serving part (what survives at $T = 0$) and a sampling part (the difference). Randomness named: at $T = 0$ with top-$k$ 64 and top-$p$ 0.95 decoding is greedy, the environment is deterministic after the action (exposure-conditioned once-guarded trigger, committed-row grader, validity voids before outcome), and frames are digest-matched step by step, so a divergence at a step with equal input digests has one remaining source, the provider's serving arithmetic (batch-dependent kernels and routing), with retries on provider error logged and excluded.
claim: An agent run at temperature 0 in an environment certified not to move on its own still diverges and flips outcomes within a 40-action episode, so the serving stack by itself is a source of benchmark variance that no replicate rule on the environment side removes.
trick: Turn the sampling off, hold the world fixed by certification, hash every observation, and count how often two runs that saw byte-identical inputs took different actions and ended differently; whatever is left is the server, not the agent and not the world.
why_now: EnvOS's released harness journals the digest of every frame and text request (CLM-BG, 'All 626 task requests are journaled with the digests of their frame and text') and its certification voids any environment-side fault before outcome, which makes the first-divergence step identifiable for the first time on an agent benchmark; Gemini's REST invoker exposes temperature where 'the Claude CLI's cannot be set' (CLM-BG configuration delta). CL-W43-J01 (2026-10-2x, thought) needs a testbed whose environment randomness is zero to separate serving from the world; existing agent benchmarks with user simulators and live tools cannot supply it.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 (zero dollars, shared with the sibling candidate): rebuild the testbed from the supplement, confirm the claims modules re-certify, capture models.get before and after. Step 1 (4 days, about $300): 10 instances x {OFF-A, ON-A} x 5 rollouts at temperature 0 (top-$p$ 0.95, top-$k$ 64, thinking 'high', high media resolution as pinned), 100 rollouts of at most 40 actions, one launch, validity classified before outcome, retried provider errors logged and the retried step excluded from the divergence reading. Compute, for each of the 10 rollout pairs per cell: the step-wise input-digest equality, the first-divergence step $d$, whether the pair is action-identical through the commit, and the pair's outcome agreement; per cell $F_{ic}$ and $\hat p_{ic}(1-\hat p_{ic})$; pooled, the distribution of $d$ and the serving share $S = \mathbb{E}_i[\hat p_{ic}(1-\hat p_{ic})]_{T=0} / \mathbb{E}_i[\hat p_{ic}(1-\hat p_{ic})]_{T=1.0}$ against the sibling matrix. Pre-registered control: 20 single-step re-sends of an archived (frame, text) pair at $T = 0$, to measure the per-call divergence rate outside the loop. Optional step 2 (not part of the kill): a Claude Sonnet 5 arm through the Anthropic API at temperature 0 with the paper's frame-file channel, reported as a harness change and never pooled.
killing_experiment.kills_if: At temperature 0, at least 90 of the 100 rollout pairs are action-identical through the commit, no cell has $F_{ic} \ge 1$, and the 20 single-step re-sends return identical actions: the serving stack contributes nothing to outcome variance on a 40-action REST-served Gemini episode, the field's belief that $T = 0$ is reproducible holds for this stack and horizon, and CL-W43-J01's 'large enough to reorder leaderboards' is dead for REST-served Gemini at this horizon and survives only for other stacks or longer horizons (a result the J01 batch-invariant probe would cite as its API-side boundary).

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment probability 0.6: with thinking 'high' the pairs diverge early, median first-divergence step $d \le 10$ of 40, fewer than half of the pairs are action-identical through the commit, and 2 to 4 of the 10 ON-A instances flip outcome across the five $T = 0$ rollouts ($F_{ic} \ge 1$), giving a serving share $S$ between 0.3 and 0.7 of the $T = 1.0$ within-cell variance; the single-step re-send control shows a per-call divergence rate under 5%, so the divergence is the compounding of rare per-call differences over the episode, not a noisy API.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: The paper pins Gemini at 'temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 64' and notes that 'a server-side change under the same strings would not be detectable' (CLM-BG configuration delta); it attributes repeated-sampling variation to the policy ('repeated-model-sampling variation', sec. 7.3). Leaderboards that report temperature-0 runs treat them as reproducible readings of the model (the premise CL-W43-J01 was written against); the pipeline's own taste record names temperature-0 determinism as 'batch arithmetic' (taste.md §2) but has no agent-loop measurement of it.
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: If temperature-0 pairs diverge and flip outcomes in a world certified not to move, then the replicate unit for any agent benchmark is the rollout even at temperature 0, 'deterministic' leaderboard entries carry a serving-noise floor that must be reported, and the three-way split of agent outcome variance (instance, sampling, serving) becomes measurable on any testbed that hashes its observations; if they do not diverge at all, the serving floor is zero for a frontier REST stack at 40 actions, J01's premise is bounded to open-weight batched serving or longer horizons, and the sibling matrix's within-cell variance is all the policy's own sampling.

identifiability: Random given: one frozen instance, one arm, one model id (models.get captured before and after the launch), temperature 0 with the paper's top-$p$ and top-$k$, one launch window. The environment is deterministic after the action and voids its own faults before outcome, so no luck term exists after the action; a divergence is attributed to serving only at a step where the two rollouts' journaled input digests (frame and text) are equal, which excludes any rendered wall-clock drift or memo difference, and a retried provider error is logged and its step excluded. The quantity is a property of (model id, provider stack, horizon), not of the agent's policy, which is the Gate 0 point: it reads how much of 'the agent's spread' is the server. Thinking tokens are not archived by the invoker; the reading is on actions, so a thinking-level divergence that returns the same action is counted as no divergence, which makes the reported rate a lower bound on token-level nondeterminism and exactly the rate that matters for outcomes.

title: The residency cliff: the sign of context trimming's prefill cost flips with serving concurrency
statement: Replay the card paper's recorded mini-SWE-agent trajectories (fallback: the Complexity Trap's released SWE-agent trajectories, HF dataset JetBrains-Research/the-complexity-trap, per the W43 kill record) through one open engine (vLLM or SGLang, prefix cache on, least-recently-used eviction) as $N$ closed-loop sessions that each wait $W$ seconds between calls, for $N \in \{8, 16, 32, 64, 128\}$, $W \in \{0, 20\}$ s and two KV budgets $B$ (full device, half device), under four serializations of the same recorded histories: identity (the Eager arm), per-turn masking $L_5$ re-applied to Eager's recorded history, the recorded Mask-5 trajectories, and an edit-on-miss oracle that applies $L_5$ only on the calls the server reports as cache misses (the server's per-request cached-token count is the input the paper's $L_5$ never sees, card information_asymmetry (2)). Read, from the server counters, the hit fraction $h = T_{\mathrm{hit}} / T_{\mathrm{prompt}}$, executed prefill $T_{\mathrm{uncached}}$ per task, prefill and decode seconds, and tasks per GPU-hour, and test the one-line law that $h$ collapses from its single-tenant value to the shared-system-prompt share once the sessions' working sets no longer fit: $$h(N) \approx h_1\,\mathbb{1}[N \bar s \le B] + h_{\mathrm{sys}}\,\mathbb{1}[N \bar s > B],$$ where $h_1$ is the single-request hit fraction (0.96 for Eager, 0.53 for Mask-5, card sec. 4.3), $h_{\mathrm{sys}}$ the share of a prompt that is the system prompt every session re-references, $\bar s$ a session's peak resident context in KV bytes (peak prompt tokens times the engine's KV bytes per token), and $\mathbb{1}[\cdot]$ the indicator. Step 0 ($0) computes from the trajectories alone: $\bar s$ per serialization, the exact longest-common-prefix executed prefill (which also splits the paper's +608.5% into its fixed-sequence cache term and its trajectory term, card weakest_component (2)), the LRU stack-distance prediction of $h(N, B)$, and $N \bar s / B$ for the rollout configurations FlashNext-RL (2610.28998: 1,024 rollouts, 131,072-token limit, three inference nodes) and MISA-T (2608.11152) publish.
claim: The sign of a context policy's executed-prefill cost is a property of the serving regime, not of the policy: below the residency cliff $N \bar s = B$ per-turn trimming multiplies recomputed prefill, above it trimming is the only policy that reduces it, and the rollout configurations agentic-RL systems papers publish sit above the cliff.
trick: Run the same agent transcripts through one server as more and more simultaneous sessions and watch for the point where the prefix cache can no longer hold them all: below it, dropping old observations every turn multiplies the prefill the server recomputes; above it, every session recomputes its whole prompt anyway and dropping observations is the only thing that saves any.
why_now: The card paper (2610.34763, 2026-10-26) is the first to measure executed prefill, KV time-area and joules for context policies and to write the masking penalty as $-75.1\mathrm{k} + 135.9\mathrm{k}\cdot\rho$ tokens per attempt with $\rho$ the reuse fraction a runtime serves (sec. 5), then leave $\rho$ at its single-request ceiling: 'batching, cache pressure, and cloud GPUs remain untested' (sec. 7). Three papers in the last eleven weeks supply the other half without the context-policy axis: 2610.22863 (2026-10-16) replays Microsoft M365 traces under KV budgets and finds 'at one tenth of the busiest hour's demand, LRU eviction makes 63% of Deep Research calls recompute' (abstract, fetched); MISA-T (2608.11152, 2026-08-11) builds 'residency-time-aware KV accounting' and admission for mixed RL rollouts because 'KV-residency times create substantially different serving demands' (abstract, fetched); WAKMan (2610.36355, 2026-10-26) finds 'agentic steps return within seconds and favor recency' and that one workload parameter flips the best eviction policy (abstract, fetched). Enabling pieces: open engines return per-request cached-token counts (vLLM and SGLang usage fields, the counters the card reads), and released trajectory corpora (the card's artifacts at github.com/sysevol-ai/CodeNib; the Complexity Trap tarballs; Open-SWE-Traces 2606.16038). The law itself is the 1970 stack-distance result for LRU under a cyclic reference pattern (Mattson, Gecsei, Slutz and Traiger); nothing newer is needed, and that is recorded as the flag.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 ($0, 2 days): from the recorded trajectories compute per serialization (identity, $L_5$ re-applied, recorded Mask-5, $L_{10}$ for the Complexity Trap window) the per-call prompt token sequence, the exact longest-common-prefix hit tokens at $N = 1$ (reproducing the card's 96% and 53%), the peak working set $\bar s$ in tokens, and an LRU stack-distance simulation of $h(N, B)$ with the engine's block size; compute $N \bar s / B$ for FlashNext-RL and MISA-T from their stated batch, context limit, inference GPU count and model KV layout. Step 1 (replay, about 50 GPU-hours on one 80 GB H100, or the DGX Spark the card used): serve a 27B-class open model in FP8 (the card's Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 or a smaller stand-in; KV bytes per token read from the server config) with prefix caching on; drive $N$ closed-loop sessions, each sending its recorded prompts in order, decoding to the recorded output length with content discarded, then idling $W$ seconds; sweep $N \in \{8, 16, 32, 64, 128\}$, $W \in \{0, 20\}$ s, $B \in \{B_{\mathrm{full}}, B_{\mathrm{full}}/2\}$, four serializations, two seeded session orderings; about 90 sweep points at 20-40 minutes each. Record per request the server's cached-token count and prompt tokens, prefill and decode wall seconds, and per sweep point tasks per GPU-hour. Readouts: $h(N)$ per arm against the step-0 prediction; the crossover $N^{\times}$ where the $L_5$ arm's executed prefill falls below the identity arm's; the throughput ratio Mask-5 : Eager below and above the cliff; the edit-on-miss oracle as the bound on what cache-aware edit scheduling (CADOC, TokenPilot, Self-GC) recovers in each regime; the prefill share of GPU seconds per regime (a readout for CL-W43-07).
killing_experiment.kills_if: At $N = 128$, $W = 20$ s and $B = B_{\mathrm{full}}/2$, the identity (Eager) arm's hit fraction stays above 0.55 (the card's break-even) and the $L_5$ arm's executed prefill stays above the identity arm's: the LRU prefix cache holds agent working sets through tool waits at every concurrency a single engine runs, the trimming penalty is regime-independent, residency shows up only as admission queueing and never as recompute, the claim's rollout mechanism is dead, and the card's single-tenant number is the deployment number (a citable footnote: 2610.22863's 63% recompute is a fleet-placement effect, not a per-engine one). Dead as a law but kept as a measurement if a crossover exists but sits more than a factor of 2 from $B / \bar s$ at both budgets. The third clause of the claim dies on its own if step 0 puts both published rollout configurations below $N \bar s / B = 1$.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment probability 0.55 for the full set, 0.75 for the cliff alone: the identity arm's hit fraction falls from about 0.9 to below 0.4 within a factor of 2 in $N$ around $N^* = B / \bar s$ (for a 27B-class FP8 model on 80 GB and SWE-bench Verified sessions peaking near 15k tokens, step 0 puts $N^*$ in the tens of sessions per GPU; the exact number is read, not guessed); above the cliff the $L_5$ arm's executed prefill is 25-35% below the identity arm's (the prompt-volume gap, 150.5k vs 225.6k tokens per attempt, card Table 2) and its tasks per GPU-hour 1.2-1.5x higher, while below the cliff it is 0.6-0.75x (the card's +36.9% wall time); the edit-on-miss oracle matches the better arm in each regime; and FlashNext-RL's published configuration (1,024 rollouts at up to 131k tokens over three inference nodes) sits above $N \bar s / B = 1$ unless its engine offloads KV.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: Stable residency. Card sec. 5: the masking penalty is first-order $-75.1\mathrm{k} + 135.9\mathrm{k}\cdot\rho$ and sec. 7: 'Results cover two stacks on one DGX Spark serving one request at a time; batching, cache pressure, and cloud GPUs remain untested.' CADOC sec. 3.2 (W43 kill record): 'We assume stable prefix caching, no retrieval, and an indefinitely continuing stream.' TurnCost sec. 7: providers 'evict them after a time-to-live, and lose reuse when requests move between backends, none of which we model.' The serving-cost lane's verdict (card, CADOC, TokenPilot, 2607.12161) is therefore 'keep the history, the cache is cheap'; the RL systems side (FlashNext-RL abstract) reports tokens per second per GPU and iteration minutes with no hit fraction at all.
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: If the cliff is where the law puts it and published rollouts sit above it: the 'trimming costs more' results are single-tenant results that do not transfer to RL rollouts, every context-management cost column needs its regime ($N \bar s / B$) stated, agentic-RL rollout concurrency per GPU is sized by $B / \bar s$ or the context policy is chosen to move the cliff, and MISA-T-style admission and observation masking become the same lever seen from two sides. If no cliff appears within a single engine's reach: residency binds through admission queueing rather than recompute, the card's number is the deployment number, and CL-W43-12's rollout half is reworded from prefill to idle sessions (FlashNext-RL's 'a third of sessions idle').

scorecard.target_value: In print: card sec. 7 lists batching and cache pressure as untested and sec. 5 leaves $\rho$ unmeasured; 2610.22863 (abstract): 'About 80% of context tokens are served from the prefix cache' in production and LRU makes 63% of calls recompute at one tenth of peak demand; MISA-T (abstract): rollout sessions' 'KV-residency times create substantially different serving demands'; WAKMan (abstract): 'even a single workload parameter can flip the winner'. Who pays: RL infrastructure teams sizing rollout sessions per GPU (FlashNext-RL, MISA-T, prime-rl and verl users); harness teams choosing a context default for training rollouts versus API serving; the systems groups (CADOC, TokenPilot, AKV, SmoothAgent) whose 'protect the cache' motivation is regime-bound; anyone reporting an executed-prefill or dollar column for a context policy.

impact_ceiling.floor: A regime label on the card's and CADOC's results ('single-tenant') plus the measured cliff on one engine, one model and one budget; a footnote the context-cost papers cite. Requires step 0 and the sweep at one budget. Judgment p 0.40.
impact_ceiling.middle: The cliff law validated on two engines (vLLM, SGLang) and two budgets, the $N \bar s / B$ ruler applied to the published rollout configurations, and a recipe consequence (trim above the cliff, admit below it) adopted as a default in one open RL framework's rollout configuration. Requires step 1 plus a second engine (about 30 more GPU-hours). Judgment p 0.35.
impact_ceiling.ceiling: Every context-management evaluation reports executed prefill with its regime; rollout concurrency in agentic RL is sized by the residency cliff; the lane's cost accounting splits into a below-cliff (cache-priced) and an above-cliff (prefill-priced) regime with one crossover number per model and device. Requires a live RL run instrumented at the rollout engine (lab position) and a second workload family (browsing agents). Judgment p 0.15.
