title: Drift or diffusion: the growth law of the prefix log-ratio separates arithmetic mismatch from cache-eviction mismatch
statement: On teacher-forced replays of recorded agent trajectories, compute per policy token $\delta_t := \log q_{\mathrm{text}}(x_t \mid \tilde{h}_t) - \log r_{\mathrm{exec}}(x_t \mid \mathcal{C}_t)$ (the trainer's recompute from the text it sees, $\tilde{h}_t$, minus the engine's own log-probability of the token it sampled from its state $\mathcal{C}_t$) under two mismatch sources on the same model and the same trajectories: arithmetic (the card paper's stack, vLLM FP8 W8A8 plus per-token FP8 KV cache with the full cache, against a BF16 HF forward on the same text; and BF16 engine against BF16 HF as the floor) and conditioning (the AKV engine's served state after drop and repos against contiguous re-prefill of the retained text, both BF16). Remove the Gibbs drift from the prefix sum, $M_n := E_n - n\,\bar{\delta}$ with $E_n := \sum_{u \le n} \delta_u$, $n$ the number of policy tokens since the episode start (arithmetic arm) or since the last drop (eviction arm), and $\bar{\delta}$ the arm mean, and fit the growth exponent $H$ in $\mathrm{Var}[M_n] \propto n^{2H}$ across trajectories at fixed $n$. Also report the fraction of tokens whose raw $E_n$ lies outside InterQ-RL's envelope $[-\epsilon_{\mathrm{low}} \sqrt{n}, \epsilon_{\mathrm{high}} \sqrt{n}]$ (eq. 5, $\epsilon_{\mathrm{low}} = 0.025$, $\epsilon_{\mathrm{high}} = 0.05$) in each arm.
claim: Rollout-trainer mismatch from arithmetic and mismatch from KV-cache eviction have different growth laws: once the Gibbs drift is removed, the arithmetic prefix log-ratio spreads as $\sqrt{n}$ (diffusive, $H \approx 1/2$) while the post-eviction prefix log-ratio grows as $n$ (ballistic, $H \to 1$), so the exponent read from the log-probabilities a trainer already stores says which mismatch a run has, and a $\sqrt{n}$ envelope sized for the first truncates the second.
trick: Add up, token by token, how much the trainer and the engine disagree about the words the agent wrote: rounding noise piles up like a random walk, a missing piece of context pushes every later token the same way, and the slope of the pile-up tells the two apart.
why_now: InterQ-RL (2610.35303, October 2026) writes the rollout-learner ratio as a history factor times a current-token factor (card, eq. 3-4) and bounds the history factor with the $\sqrt{n_t}$ envelope it borrows from CTPO (2605.07331, May 2026), whose abstract states the design assumption in its own words: clip bounds scale 'according to the natural $\sqrt{t}$ growth of the cumulative log-ratio'. AKV (2610.28577, October 2026) ships an engine that teacher-forces any cache-operation history in one prefill, so the eviction arm is a configuration, not a kernel. The identity behind the drift, $\mathbb{E}_{x_t \sim r_{\mathrm{exec}}}[\delta_t] = -D_{\mathrm{KL}}(r_{\mathrm{exec}} \,\|\, q_{\mathrm{text}})$ (Gibbs' inequality; the card's eq. 11 is its estimator), is textbook, and the flag is recorded that nothing in the readout is new beyond the pairing.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 (zero GPU, one day, written before any run): with $\mathbb{E}[\delta_t] = -\mathrm{KL}$ per token, the expected raw prefix sum after $n$ tokens is $-n \cdot \mathrm{KL}$ and crosses InterQ-RL's lower envelope $-\epsilon_{\mathrm{low}} \sqrt{n}$ at $n^{*} = (\epsilon_{\mathrm{low}} / \mathrm{KL})^{2}$; with the card's K3 anchors (sec. 3.1, median over the final 20 steps) this gives $n^{*} < 1$ token at the aligned-quantized level ($\mathrm{KL} \approx 0.029$) and $n^{*} \approx 319$ tokens at the BF16 level ($\mathrm{KL} \approx 0.0014$). Prediction: in the paper's own regime the lower clip binds in expectation from the first policy token and the history weight reduces to $\overline{W}_t = \exp(-0.025 \sqrt{n_t})$, a depth discount. Step 1 (about 30 GPU-h, 5 days): 60 trajectories of Qwen3-8B (the card paper's ScienceWorld model; GPT-OSS-20B if the AKV fork serves only that family, in which case the arithmetic arm runs on the same model in vLLM BF16 versus FP8-KV only) on SWE-bench Verified with mini-SWE-agent under AKV's drop-all-but-the-latest-12 tool responses with repos, temperature 1.0 as in the paper, operation sequence and engine log-probs logged (reuse C-W43-25's 90 recorded trajectories if they exist). Five teacher-forced passes per trajectory: vLLM FP8 W8A8 plus FP8 E4M3 per-token KV on the full text (the paper's rollout config, App. C.1), vLLM BF16 on the full text, HF BF16 on the full text, AKV served state under the recorded operations, AKV contiguous re-prefill of the retained text. Form $\delta^{N}_t$ (FP8 engine minus HF), $\delta^{0}_t$ (BF16 engine minus HF) and $\delta^{E}_t$ (served state minus text state); per arm compute $\bar{\delta}$, $M_n$, $\mathrm{Var}[M_n]$ across trajectories at $n \in \{8, 16, 32, \ldots, 1024\}$ (clock reset at each drop in the eviction arm), the least-squares slope $2H$ on log-log axes with a bootstrap band over trajectories, the lag-$k$ autocorrelation of $\delta_t$ for $k \le 64$ (the mechanism: $H > 1/2$ is positively correlated increments), the envelope-exceedance fraction, and $\bar{\delta}$ in K3 units against the paper's three anchors (1.03 unaligned, 0.029 aligned, 0.0014 BF16).
killing_experiment.kills_if: The fitted exponents $H^{E}$ (post-drop) and $H^{N}$ (arithmetic, same model) agree within 0.1 with overlapping bootstrap bands, on the centred sums: eviction mismatch accumulates like arithmetic mismatch, the exponent does not discriminate, and a $\sqrt{n}$-envelope correction fed by log-probabilities alone (InterQ-RL, CTPO) covers the eviction term too, which withdraws the 'log the operation sequence' consequence of CL-W43-11 and leaves the claim its ghost-information half (C-W43-24). That negative is citable on its own. Established if $H^{E} \geq H^{N} + 0.25$ with disjoint bands. Separately, step 0's prediction is refuted if fewer than half of the arithmetic-arm tokens at $n > 50$ sit on the lower envelope boundary, in which case the clip is a correction as the paper says and the depth-discount reading is dropped.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment probability 0.55: $H^{N} \in [0.5, 0.65]$ after centring (rounding errors weakly correlated; the FP8 KV write persists, so some memory), $H^{E} \in [0.8, 1.0]$ over the first 200 policy tokens after a drop and decaying toward 0.5 as the dropped content stops mattering; the arithmetic arm's raw $E_n$ sits on the lower envelope for more than 80% of tokens past $n = 50$. Probability 0.25: both exponents near 1 (persistent FP8 KV error makes arithmetic mismatch ballistic too), the ruler is dead and the $\sqrt{n}$ envelope is wrong for both. Probability 0.20: both near 0.5, the probe kills.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: CTPO's abstract: 'position-adaptive clipping that scales log-space clip bounds according to the natural $\sqrt{t}$ growth of the cumulative log-ratio'. title: Does the eviction term reach the gradient: text recompute, InterQ-RL weights and operation-aware recompute on the same rollouts
statement: Take two batches $\mathcal{B}$, $\mathcal{B}'$ of 64 agent rollouts each (8 prompts times 8 responses, GRPO group-normalized advantages from official test rewards), sampled under KV-cache eviction on the AKV engine (drop all but the latest 12 tool responses, then repos) with Qwen3-8B on SWE-bench Verified, the operation sequence and the engine's per-token log-probabilities logged. At the sampling checkpoint compute the policy gradient three ways from the same rollouts and rewards: $g_{\mathrm{text}}$ (the trainer recomputes from the retained text prefilled contiguously, today's practice), $g_{\mathrm{IQ}}$ (the same, with InterQ-RL's history weights $W_t$ from eqs. 5-9 computed from the engine's logged log-probabilities and the text recompute), and $g_{\mathrm{op}}$ (the trainer reproduces the engine's conditioning with a block attention mask and the repositioned position ids, so each token attends to exactly what the engine attended to; the trainer-side twin of AKV's segment-batch attention). Measure the bias $\|g_{\mathrm{text}} - g_{\mathrm{op}}\|$ and $\|g_{\mathrm{IQ}} - g_{\mathrm{op}}\|$ against the batch's own sampling noise $\sigma := \|g_{\mathrm{op}}(\mathcal{B}) - g_{\mathrm{op}}(\mathcal{B}')\| / \sqrt{2}$, the cosine between the two batches' bias vectors, and the same ratio at sub-batch sizes 16 and 32.
claim: At the batch sizes agentic GRPO trains with, recomputing log-probabilities from the text of rollouts that were served under KV eviction biases the policy gradient by an amount comparable to the batch's sampling noise and in a direction that repeats across batches, and the history-level correction that fixes quantization mismatch removes less than a third of it because it is sized for a diffusing, not a drifting, log-ratio.
trick: Compute the training update three ways from the same episodes: pretending the text is what the model saw, applying the quantization paper's fix, and rebuilding exactly what the model saw; then ask whether the pretend update differs from the exact one by more than the dice do.
why_now: AKV (2610.28577, October 2026) ships an engine that logs the operation sequence and reconstructs any operation history in one prefill, which is the specification for the trainer-side mask in $g_{\mathrm{op}}$; InterQ-RL (2610.35303, October 2026) gives a history-level weight computable from log-probabilities alone, so the question 'does a shipped correction absorb the eviction term' can be asked without training; the Zero-Mismatch Reference (2605.14220, May 2026) shows that 'small token-level numerical disagreements can independently cause training collapse', which makes the size of a larger, structured term at the gradient a live question; import:2026-W43-S6xF7 predicts KV residency binds agentic-RL throughput, so eviction inside rollouts is the next lever systems teams ship.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 (about 5 GPU-h, 3 days of engineering): implement the operation-aware recompute as one HF forward with a 4-D attention mask (tokens generated before a drop attend to the dropped tool response; tokens after it do not) and position ids that follow the repos; validate it by checking that its token log-probabilities match the engine's logged values at the BF16 floor (K3 at the 0.0014 level, card sec. 3.1) and that, before the first drop in every episode, $g_{\mathrm{text}}$ and $g_{\mathrm{op}}$ agree to the batch-arithmetic floor (a built-in null; if it fails, the reproduction is wrong and the probe stops). Step 1 (about 55 GPU-h, 6 days): sample the two batches (about 40 GPU-h on 2 H100-class GPUs, episodes capped at 100 steps with the effective context set so that drops fire in most episodes), then compute the three gradients per batch with backprop over all parameters and no optimizer step (gradient at $\theta = \theta_{\mathrm{old}}$, so PPO clipping is inactive and $g = \sum_{\tau} \sum_{t} A_{\tau} m_t \nabla_{\theta} \log q_{\theta}(x_t \mid \cdot)$ with $A_{\tau}$ the group-normalized advantage and $m_t$ the policy-token mask), repeating $g_{\mathrm{op}}$ once to record the batch-arithmetic floor. Readouts: $\beta_{\mathrm{text}} := \|g_{\mathrm{text}} - g_{\mathrm{op}}\| / \sigma$ and $\beta_{\mathrm{IQ}}$ likewise; the cross-batch cosine $c$ between $g_{\mathrm{text}}(\mathcal{B}) - g_{\mathrm{op}}(\mathcal{B})$ and the same vector on $\mathcal{B}'$; the removal fraction $1 - \beta_{\mathrm{IQ}} / \beta_{\mathrm{text}}$; all three per layer and split by tokens before versus after the first drop; $\beta_{\mathrm{text}}$ at sub-batch sizes 16, 32, 64, since $\sigma$ falls as $1/\sqrt{N}$ and a bias does not.
killing_experiment.kills_if: $\beta_{\mathrm{text}} < 0.25$ and $|c| < 0.2$ on both batches at $N = 64$: the eviction term does not reach the gradient at training batch sizes, text recompute is adequate under this drop policy, and CL-W43-11's trainer half is a per-token curiosity with no training consequence (citable as: cache eviction inside rollouts needs no trainer change at $K = 12$). Established if $\beta_{\mathrm{text}} \geq 0.5$ and $c \geq 0.5$. The InterQ-RL arm is read separately: a removal fraction above $2/3$ means a shipped log-probability-only correction suffices and the operation log is unnecessary; below $1/3$ it does not.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment probability 0.50: $\beta_{\mathrm{text}} \in [0.5, 1.5]$ at $N = 64$, rising with $N$, $c > 0.5$, and InterQ-RL's weights remove under a third of the bias (its raw prefix sum sits on the lower clip, so the weight is a depth discount that carries no information about the drop's direction). Probability 0.30: the bias is small and unstructured, the probe kills. Probability 0.20: the bias is large and InterQ-RL's weights remove most of it, so log-probabilities suffice and the operation log is not needed.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: InterQ-RL, sec. 3.2 (card): the rollout-learner discrepancy is 'two evaluations of the same checkpoint along different numerical paths', and the trainer's input is 'all turns of an episode ... as one concatenated sequence' (App. C.1). AKV names 'training agents under this scheme' as future work (sec. 6, per card 2610.28577). The Zero-Mismatch Reference: mismatch 'should be treated as a first-order factor in analyzing LLM RL stability', measured for the arithmetic case only. Agentic-RL stacks record token sequences as the trajectory (C-W43-25's stated assumption, to be verified against their code at the kill search).
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: Established: the trajectory record for evicting rollouts must carry the operation sequence, or trainers must forbid eviction; shipped log-probability corrections do not substitute; this is the gradient-level consequence CL-W43-11 needs before any training comparison. Killed: cache eviction is a free serving lever inside RL at this drop policy, which unblocks CL-W43-12's KV-residency lever without a trainer change, and no InterQ-RL-style correction is needed for eviction either. Bias large but removed by InterQ-RL's weights: the operation log is unnecessary and the claim's consequence shrinks to 'use a history-level weight', which changes what CL-W43-11 asks of trainers.

scorecard.target_value: In print: AKV's future-work sentence on training under cache operations; InterQ-RL's admission that no scalar says when history-level correction is needed (sec. 4.2); the Zero-Mismatch Reference's 'first-order factor'. Who pays: agentic-RL infrastructure teams (verl, SkyRL, prime-rl and the others named in import S6xF7) deciding whether eviction is allowed inside rollouts; serving-engine teams deciding whether to expose the operation log; users of the FP8-RL stack who would otherwise reach for InterQ-RL's weights.

impact_ceiling.middle: A structured bias comparable to the sampling noise, a batch-size curve, and the trainer-side operation-aware recompute (one HF forward with a block mask) as the shipped artifact, adopted by one open stack; requires step 1; judgment p 0.45.
impact_ceiling.ceiling: The training comparison (KV-drop rollouts with text recompute, with operation-aware recompute, and TEXT-drop rollouts with exact recompute, about 150 GPU-h, lab position) shows the biased arm regressing late as InterQ-RL's alignment-only arm did (95.5% to 89.6% between steps 300 and 400, sec. 4.2); operation logs become a standard field of agentic-RL trajectory records; judgment p 0.25.

title: Where message-attributable handoff failures sit: dropped, in view and unused, or followed from an invented entry — the census with its full-history pair
statement: On HSC-Bench's continuation track (739 tasks x 6 receivers; the sheet, transcript-tail and full-history arms are already run for all six, Table 2; the authors' outputs are requested first) and on Compact-Bench's public paired full-history / summary-only continuations (2610.31710) as the corpus that needs no email, take every criterion a receiver fails under the handoff message and passes under full history, and label it with the benchmark's own typed matcher: the needed value was dropped (in the source history, not in the message), corrupted (a different sourced value in its field), in view and unused (in the message, sourced, and still not reported), or followed from an unsourced entry (the receiver's reported value equals a message entry that matches nothing in the source history); criteria failed under both arms are the receiver's baseline and are reported beside the cells. A placebo message from another task of the same scenario family gives the chance-match rate of every cell, intervals are bootstrapped over scenario families, and the unsourced-entry share of every message is published first so the followed-unsourced cell is read against its base rate. The repository track (300 ContextBench-annotated tasks on public CodeTraceBench GPT-5 trajectories) is the fallback if no continuation data are shared: there the typed values are file paths, the oracle is the gold annotation, and the full-history arm is ours to run.
claim: Fewer than one in ten message-attributable handoff failures — a criterion failed under the 1,600-character sheet and passed under full history by the same receiver — are the receiver acting on an entry the writer invented; the remainder are a needed value the sheet dropped or a value in view that the receiver did not use.
trick: Pair each handoff failure with the same receiver's full-history run, keep only the failures the message caused, and sort them by whether the needed fact was dropped, left unused, or replaced by something the writer made up.
why_now: HSC-Bench (2026-10-27) ran the full-history arm for all six receivers on 739 typed-criterion tasks (sec. 4.1, Table 2) and never computed per-entry provenance; Compact-Bench (2026-10-22) released paired full-history / summary-only continuations with code and data; the C-W43-23 red team (2026-10-25) wrote down the uncompressed control and the typed matcher this census needs and found both absent on AppWorld. The three pieces landed within two weeks; the flag is that the lane produced about eight compaction papers in the same two weeks.

killing_experiment.kills_if: For at least three of six receivers the family-clustered 95% lower bound of $\pi_{\mathrm{inv}}$ among message-attributable failures is above 0.10 and above the placebo chance-match rate: the writer's invented entries are a main cause of handoff failure, CL-W43-05's mechanism carries from iterative compaction to one-shot handoff sheets, and this census is its second benchmark. An interval straddling 0.10 is reported as such and settles nothing. Protocol kill: if more than 25% of message-attributable failures are unclassifiable under the typed matcher (composed or derived values), the probe parks with that number.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment probability 0.6: $\pi_{\mathrm{inv}} < 0.10$ for every receiver, with unsourced entries under 15% of sheet entries and concentrated in remaining-work fields; in-view-unused is the largest cell (0.4-0.6) on tool and file-work tasks and dropped the largest on conversational tasks; the placebo chance-match rate is under 0.05 under typed matching.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: CL-W43-05's current belief, from SJC 2610.20927: 25 of 35 analysed compaction failures (71%) follow a summary entry no environment output supports or that contradicts one. The card's paper assumes the opposite without a count: 'The failure occurs after the necessary completion information has reached the receiver' (sec. 5.4) and 'these results highlight the importance of how the receiver uses the supplied information to determine what to do next' (sec. 5.5), resting on 2 repeats of 114 continuations.
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: If following an invented entry is under a tenth of message-caused failures, the provenance gate is the wrong first lever for handoff messages and the lane's ruler needs a use axis (in view and unused) that no published handoff or compaction score has. If it is above a quarter, unsourced persistence is a property of LLM-written state regardless of write regime, and SJC's gate belongs in every handoff writer.

identifiability: Random given: the task, the recorded source history, the fixed messages (one GPT-4.1 sheet and one transcript tail per task), temperature 0 and top-$p$ 1 at each receiver (App. A), so the (sheet, full) pair differs only in the message and provider nondeterminism; the cells are properties of the (writer, receiver, benchmark) triple and are reported as such, never as 'handoffs' in general. The matcher is the benchmark's own criterion rule typed by field, so a bare integer in the wrong field does not match, and chance membership is measured by the placebo, not assumed. The reference-leak rule (the receiver supplies the reference when the history has none) is excluded by construction. No judge: the 150-label audit checks the matcher, not a labeler. Full history is the control that C-W43-23 lacked: under it every value is in view, so 'dropped' is zero by construction and the paired difference isolates the message.

Lab: the HSC authors hold the 739-task track and the outputs and can compute the cells in a day; the re-open test is the email. title: Unsourced entries by write regime: the same writer and budget, iterating on its own summary versus rewriting from the raw log
statement: On the rebuilt HSC repository track (300 public CodeTraceBench GPT-5 histories, ten action-observation pairs each) and on SJC's AppWorld harness (147 train+dev tasks x 3 runs, 4,096-token window, the only split with reference solutions), produce at every boundary two messages at the same character budget from the same writer and prompt: iterative (the writer sees its previous summary plus the steps since, as compaction does) and one-shot (the writer sees the whole raw history to that point, as the card's handoff writer does). Label every entry sourced or unsourced with the typed matcher against the raw history, and report the unsourced-entry share per message by regime and boundary index, the retention of later-needed typed values (annotated paths; AppWorld needed values from the reference solutions' state-changing calls), and the receiver's score under each message (line-F1; AppWorld accuracy and Pass3). The matched quantities are the writer, the prompt, the budget and the boundary.
claim: Unsourced entries in compaction summaries are made by iterating on a prior summary: at the same budget and boundary, the same writer rewriting from the raw log produces fewer than half as many entries that match nothing in the history.
trick: Compact the same trajectory twice, once by updating the old summary and once from scratch off the raw log, and count which one invents more.
why_now: SJC (2026-10-14) counted unsourced entries only in the iterative regime (13-21% of entries pruned, Open TODOs 67.7% unsourced, per the C-W43-08 record); the card's paper (2026-10-27) ran only the one-shot regime and never counted; 'Benchmarks Are Surprisingly Compaction-Friendly' (2610.31778, 2026-10-22) measured the omission side of the regime effect, dropped constraints rising 'monotonically with the number of compactions', and the commission side is unmeasured. The raw log is always on disk, so the one-shot arm is a free recipe if the count favours it.

killing_experiment.design: Repository track: for each of 300 histories, boundaries after steps 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10. Iterative arm: GPT-4.1 given (previous sheet, steps since the last boundary) writes a 1,800-character sheet; one-shot arm: GPT-4.1 given all steps to the boundary writes a 1,800-character sheet; same prompt otherwise (ours, published). 1,500 writer calls per arm, about 9M tokens each, about $25 per arm. Typed matcher on paths, symbols, line numbers and command strings against the raw history gives $u_{b}^{(\mathrm{iter})}$ and $u_{b}^{(\mathrm{one})}$, the unsourced share of entries at boundary $b$. Receivers: six at the step-10 boundary under each sheet (300 x 6 x 2 single calls, under $40), scored by line-F1 against ContextBench gold; retention of annotated paths per arm (the paper's $\rho$, sec. 5.3). AppWorld: SJC's harness with a second compaction method, raw-rewrite (one-shot from the full logged trajectory at each harness-triggered boundary, same OpenClaw prompt and budget), against the stock iterative compressor; 147 tasks x 3 runs per arm at 112.8K tokens per task, $110-150 per arm at GPT-5.6 Luna list price (C-W43-23 red team's figure); the iterative arm is free if SJC's authors share Prompting-arm logs. Readouts: $\bar u$ per regime with boundary-indexed curves, the ratio $\rho_u = \bar u^{(\mathrm{iter})} / \bar u^{(\mathrm{one})}$ with family (repository) or scenario (AppWorld) cluster bootstrap, the split of unsourced entries into identifiers versus plans to compare with SJC's Table 2, retention of later-needed values per arm, and receiver scores per arm.
killing_experiment.kills_if: The cluster-bootstrapped 95% upper bound of $\rho_u$ is below 2 on both corpora: iterating on a prior summary does not multiply unsourced entries, the writer invents at the same rate from the raw log, and the provenance gate rather than re-compaction from raw is the lever, a citable negative for every harness that keeps the raw log. A second kill: if the one-shot arm retains later-needed values at a rate more than 10 points below the iterative arm at the same budget, the regime comparison is confounded by what each arm keeps and is parked with that number.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment probability 0.5: $\rho_u$ between 2 and 4 on AppWorld, driven by plan sections (Open TODOs, pending asks), near 1 for exact identifiers; under 1.5 on the repository track, where paths are copied rather than inferred; receiver scores equal within noise on both.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: SJC treats unsourced entries as a property of the summary to be gated entry by entry ('Prune the Summary, Not the History'); CL-W43-05's if_true is 'compactors label or delete unsourced entries by default'; the card's writer is one-shot and its paper never asks the question; the recursive-memory line (Wang et al. 2308.15022: 'recursively produce new memory using previous memory and following contexts') reports consistency gains and no invention count.
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: If $\rho_u \geq 2$, the cheapest compaction fix is to rewrite from the raw log instead of the prior summary, and CL-W43-05's mechanism is re-scoped to the iterative regime with its if_true changed from 'delete' to 'rewrite'. If $\rho_u < 2$, invention is the writer's and regime-independent, and SJC's gate is the lever in every regime.

identifiability: Random given: the recorded history, the writer (GPT-4.1 or the SJC compressor model) at temperature 0, the prompt and the budget; the two arms differ only in the writer's input (prior summary plus delta versus raw log). Unsourced is defined against the raw history, which both arms could in principle see, so a one-shot entry is unsourced only by invention while an iterative entry is unsourced by invention or by inheriting an earlier invention; $\rho_u$ measures inheritance plus any regime-induced invention, and the boundary-indexed curve separates them (inheritance grows with $b$, fresh invention does not). On the repository track the source history is fixed, so arms are paired at every boundary; on AppWorld the agent acts on the summary after the first boundary, so arms are paired at the first boundary and marginal after, and the record says which number is which. Retention is measured so that a regime that invents less by keeping less is caught by the second kill.

title: Re-solve what the agent shipped: the per-command physics audit on agent-written simulators
statement: Re-run the paper's released code policies (the family that succeeds on 96.7% of 2,048 gift-box states, sec. 6.3, and its siblings on five other simulations) inside the shipped simulators with full physical state logged at every command boundary, then re-solve each command from its logged start state under a refined reference (the same solver with the time step halved and the solver-iteration cap and substep count doubled, relative to the agent-chosen settings in Table 6) and compute the lane's audit $d_k = \lVert F_{\mathrm{ref}}(x_k, a_k) - x_{k+1} \rVert$ on the verifier's state coordinates, with the threshold $\kappa$ set to the verifier's own success tolerance; separately run every episode end to end under the refined settings and report the success flip $\Delta S = S_{\mathrm{ship}} - S_{\mathrm{ref}}$ with its replay-seed interval. Six simulations, one per engine family in Table 6: rigid and articulated contact on Newton 1.5 with the MuJoCo Warp solver (0.5 ms ticks; the padlock at 1,920 Hz and 64 iterations), DFSPH liquid (93,750 to 348,160 particles), MPM soil, backward-Euler cloth, explicit FEM tissue (1e-5 s substeps, 73,273 tets), and the 7.18 M-cell welding enthalpy solver. Readouts per simulation: the distribution of $d_k / \kappa$ over contact-bearing commands, the share of return on suspicious commands $\rho = \sum_k r_k \mathbb{1}[d_k > \kappa] / \sum_k r_k$, and $\Delta S$.
claim: Agent-written simulators that pass same-model audits ship at discretisations their own solution policies depend on: halving the time step at the agent-chosen settings flips at least one in ten verified successes on at least two of six engine families.
trick: Take the robot programs that solve the agent-built tasks, re-run every move with the physics computed twice as finely, and count how many solved tasks stop being solved.
why_now: The card paper (2026-10-29) is the first released corpus of simulators whose physics a coding agent wrote: 25 simulators with their solver settings tabulated (Table 6), released solution programs with privileged state (sec. 6.3), and a recorded-attempt format with launch configuration and source version (Appendix D), so re-solving visited states under a refined reference is a replay job. The lane's audit (themes.yaml L5) has existed as a spec since 2026-10-11 with no agent-written corpus to run on. The refinement test itself is textbook (halve the step, compare), which is the flag: nothing is new but the target.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 (zero dollars, 2 days): clone the release; for each of the six simulations extract the step size $h$, iteration cap $K$ and substep count $m$ from Table 6 and the launch configuration; replay one recorded attempt twice from its command log and report the batch-repeat spread $\sigma_0$ of the final state as the resolution floor (checklist 2026-10-20: a GPU-batch repeat spread is read before any $d_k$); confirm that the verifier reads a state tolerance and record it as $\kappa$ per task. Step 1 (shipped arm): run the released code policy on 50 varied initial states per simulation with the full physical state saved at every command boundary; this is the arm the paper reports. Step 2 (reference arm, per command): from each saved start state, execute the same command under $(h/2, 2K, 2m)$ and compute $d_k$ on the verifier's coordinates; a command is 'contact-bearing' if the shipped solver reports any active contact or particle-boundary interaction during it. Step 3 (reference arm, end to end): run the same 50 initial states under $(h/2, 2K, 2m)$ from start to finish and score with the unchanged verifier; $\Delta S$ with a bootstrap interval over initial states and over replay seeds. Step 4: a second reference at $(h/4, 4K, 4m)$ on the two simulations with the largest $d_k$, to show $d_k$ shrinks with refinement (a convergence check, not a trend read from two points). Budget: the liquids and the welding cell at up to 200x real time dominate; 50 episodes x about 20 commands x 6 simulations at two refinement levels, about 120 GPU-hours on one H100-class card.

title: Optimise against the verifier: what a budgeted search finds that three adversarial audit rounds did not
statement: On four of the 25 simulations (two whose shared audit memory and reports record no remaining defect after round three, two whose recorded defect was fixed; Appendix B), run a budgeted derivative-free search (CMA-ES over the released code policy's waypoint, timing and force parameters, 600 episodes per task, privileged state as the paper's own learning studies allow) that maximises the state-based verifier's reward $r \in [0,1]$, and audit every verifier success with four physics invariants that need no reference engine: maximum interpenetration depth, conservation of particle mass and volume for liquids and soil, mechanical energy gained without actuator work, and the per-command refinement check $d_k$ of the sibling candidate. Report the physically invalid success share $\epsilon = \frac{\#\{\text{success} \wedge \text{violation}\}}{\#\{\text{success}\}}$ for the optimised programs against the same share for the released honest programs, with violation thresholds set at the 99th percentile of the honest programs' trajectories, and the recall of the paper's adversarial auditor: the share of violation classes the optimiser reaches that appear in that simulation's audit report or the shared memory.
claim: Adversarial LLM auditing before optimisation misses what a budgeted optimiser finds after it: in agent-written simulators that passed three audit rounds, a 600-episode search against the state-based verifier makes at least one in ten verified successes physically invalid.
trick: Instead of asking a model to imagine how a robot could cheat the simulator, let a cheap optimiser try to maximise the task score, then check whether its winning runs broke mass, energy or solid walls.
why_now: The card paper (2026-10-29) is the first corpus where an adversary's findings are written down per simulation before release (the adversarial auditor 'found a real defect in about three quarters of our simulations', sec. 6.4; the shared memory records 'colliders that passed audits and appeared in renders while having no physical effect', Appendix B), so an auditor's recall against an optimiser is computable for the first time; the released solution programs give the optimiser a parametrised starting point so no policy has to be learned. Policy-Aware Simulator Learning (2605.29032, abstract fetched 2026-11-01) states for learned simulators that 'powerful RL optimizers inevitably exploit minor model inaccuracies' and that the worst-case policy is dual to RL on one-step error; the engineered-simulator version with a written pre-release audit to score against is what this corpus supplies.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 (zero dollars, 2 days): read the 25 audit reports and the shared memory (Appendix B) and tabulate, per simulation, the defect classes found and fixed and the round-three verdict; choose two simulations recorded defect-free and two with a fixed defect, spanning rigid contact, liquid and cloth; read each verifier to confirm it scores state, not images. Step 1 (honest arm): run the released code policy on 200 varied initial states per simulation with full state logged; compute the four invariants per trajectory and set each violation threshold at the honest arm's 99th percentile (so $\epsilon_{\mathrm{honest}} \le 0.01$ by construction on the calibration set; report it on a held-out 100 states). Step 2 (optimiser arm): parametrise the code policy's waypoints, timings and commanded forces (10 to 40 parameters), run CMA-ES for 600 episodes per simulation with the verifier reward as the objective and the same varied initial states, log full state, compute the invariants on every verifier success; $\epsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}$ with a bootstrap interval over episodes. Step 3 (recall): two labellers with a written rubric sort each optimiser violation into a class (interpenetration, through-collider, mass loss, energy gain, discretisation-dependent) and mark whether that class appears in the simulation's audit report or the memory; report agreement and the auditor's recall per simulation. Cost: 4 simulations x 900 episodes at about 2 minutes each (the paper's code-policy run time, sec. 6.3) plus the refinement re-solves on successes, about 100 GPU-hours.
killing_experiment.kills_if: On all four simulations $\epsilon_{\mathrm{opt}} - \epsilon_{\mathrm{honest}} < 0.05$ with the bootstrap band including zero: a 600-episode optimiser against the verifier reaches no exploit the three-round audit left, the paper's trust story holds at this budget, and the result is a positive verification of LLM adversarial auditing that the authors and anyone building creation-audit loops would cite.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment probability 0.55: $\epsilon_{\mathrm{opt}} \ge 0.1$ on at least two of four simulations including one recorded defect-free, with interpenetration and through-collider violations (the memory file's own class) the majority, and the auditor's recall below 0.5 on those two; near zero on the rigid-contact simulation where the Newton / MuJoCo Warp solver was not written by the agent.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: The card paper: 'Since reinforcement learning optimizes against the simulation, any such exploit could otherwise become learned behavior' (sec. 3), answered by an adversarial auditor with legal robot actions over three rounds whose residual miss rate is never estimated; the simulations that survive are shipped as RL environments and no RL is run on them (sec. 6, Appendix B). Policy-Aware Simulator Learning (2605.29032) assumes exploitation is inevitable for learned models and does not measure engineered ones.
preregistered_surprise.would_change: If $\epsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}$ is large: pre-release LLM auditing is a low-recall exploit search, the 200 environments need an optimiser-in-the-loop audit before RL, and the ruler the lane wants for soft bodies (where no converged reference exists) is the invariant-violation share under a budgeted optimiser, which this probe operationalises. If $\epsilon_{\mathrm{opt}} \approx 0$: three rounds of model-imagined legal actions are as good as 600 episodes of optimisation at finding exploits, which argues for the loop as a cheap verification standard and against spending GPU-hours on adversarial search for agent-audited simulators.

identifiability: Exploitable given: the budget (600 episodes), the search space (the released program's parameters) and the verifier; $\epsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}$ is a property of (simulation, verifier, parametrisation, budget) and is reported as such, never as 'the' exploitability. Violations are defined by invariants readable from the privileged state the paper exposes (penetration depth, particle counts and volumes, kinetic plus potential energy against actuator work), with thresholds from the honest arm's 99th percentile, so $\epsilon_{\mathrm{honest}}$ is near 0.01 by construction and the quantity of interest is the difference. Deterministic replay given source version, configuration and seed (Appendix D), so the optimiser's noise is the varied initial states, which both arms share. The auditor's recall depends on a class taxonomy: two labellers, a written rubric, agreement reported; a class is 'found' only if it appears in that simulation's own report or the memory text. Verifier, not judge: the objective is the state-based verifier; no LLM scores anything in this probe.
positioning_note: Solo: public code, 100 GPU-hours, an off-the-shelf optimiser. Lab: the Gym-Anything authors run the optimiser auditor as a fourth role inside the loop on all 25, which is the re-open test (ask whether they have run any optimiser against their verifiers). Operator 2 moves the exploit search from before optimisation (a model's imagination) to after it; operator 7 turns the paper's adversarial auditor into a control arm scored by recall. Not written: operator 3 (allocate audit rounds by measured exploitability) presupposes this result; a learned RL policy as the adversary was rejected because the brief forbids a new learned model and the code-policy parametrisation is cheaper.

title: Score the agent's cloth and tissue against measured reality: GAUGE's trajectory error on agent-written solvers
statement: Port three of GAUGE's measurement-grounded task families (2608.05948: one textile, one volumetric deformable, one rigid impulsive contact, each with real trajectories, calibrated material metadata and a task observable) into the shipped agent-written solvers (the backward-Euler cloth, the explicit FEM tissue, and the Newton 1.5 / MuJoCo Warp rigid stack the agent configured), feed GAUGE's calibrated parameters as inputs, and compute GAUGE's generalized trajectory error $e = \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T} \lVert q^{\mathrm{sim}}_t - q^{\mathrm{real}}_t \rVert$ over the task observable $q_t$ at the $T$ measured instants, placing each number on GAUGE's own table beside Isaac Sim, Genesis and Newton; before scoring, validate the port by reproducing GAUGE's published Newton number within 10% through the same scene files. Readouts: the agent solver's error relative to the best and worst of the three engines per family, and the error of the agent solver run at GAUGE's calibrated parameters versus at the parameters the agent chose for itself.
claim: Agent-written soft-body solvers that win 76% of same-model blind comparisons are further from measured real deformable trajectories than the shipped engines they beat, on the same real data and the same error metric.
trick: Run the agent's cloth and tissue physics on scenes where somebody filmed and measured the real material, and read its error off the same ruler three shipped engines were already scored with.
why_now: GAUGE (2608.05948, published 2026-08-06; abstract fetched 2026-11-01) supplies 'real-world trajectories ... paired with calibrated physical metadata' across 'rigid bodies, flexible cables, textiles, and volumetric deformable objects' and already scores Isaac Sim, Genesis and Newton on 14 families with 'generalized trajectory errors', so the incumbents' side of the comparison is published; the card paper (2026-10-29) supplies released soft-body solvers written by an agent and compared to incumbents only by a same-model blind judgment (sec. 6.4). The card notes the creator cites GAUGE's material tables for static parameters and never uses a measured trajectory, so the comparison is open and the inputs are already in the agent's hands.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 (zero dollars, 3 days): confirm GAUGE's release of trajectories, metadata and scene definitions for at least one textile, one volumetric-deformable and one rigid-contact family, and its exact error definition; confirm in the agent-written reports which solver each simulation uses and whether any GAUGE trajectory was used in creation or audit (the card says only static parameters were cited; this is checked, not assumed). Step 1 (port validation): build the three scenes for Newton through our own scene files and reproduce GAUGE's published Newton error within 10%; if the port misses by more, fix the port before touching the agent solver, so scene error is bounded before solver error is read. Step 2: run the agent's cloth, tissue and rigid stacks on the same scenes at GAUGE's calibrated parameters, compute $e$ per family with GAUGE's uncertainty annotations as the error bar; Step 3: repeat at the agent's self-chosen parameters from its own report to separate parameter choice from solver form. Step 4: the refinement check of the sibling candidate on the same runs, so model-form error (persists under refinement) is separated from discretisation error (shrinks under refinement). Cost: porting labour dominates; GPU use is small (tens of short scenes).
killing_experiment.kills_if: On every ported family the agent solver's error $e$ at GAUGE's calibrated parameters lies inside the range spanned by Isaac Sim, Genesis and Newton on that family (with the port validated to 10% on Newton): the headline is dead, and the result is the first evidence that an agent-written solver audited without real data reaches validated-engine parity on measured deformable trajectories, a bigger result for the paper than its own 76%, and a direct update to the lane's belief that synthesised soft-body scenes carry no measured material behaviour.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment probability 0.6: on the textile family the agent's cloth error is 1.5x to 3x the best engine's (GAUGE reports 'the largest discrepancies arising in impulsive contact, rapid textile motion, and volumetric deformation' even for shipped engines, and the agent's cloth was checked only against formulas and expected behaviour); on the rigid impulsive-contact family the agent stack lands within the engine range because the solver underneath is Newton 1.5 / MuJoCo Warp, not agent-written; the volumetric family sits between.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: The card paper: its quality evidence is a 76% physics win rate and an 80% visuals win rate from a blind comparison where 'Claude Opus 5.5 then compared each pair blind' against incumbents including RGBench and BEHAVIOR-1K (sec. 6.4, Table 2), and its physics checks test 'against theory, measurement, or expected behavior' with no simulation compared to a measured trajectory (Appendix E). The lane's standing belief (CL-W43-J06 thread, 2026-10-23 session) is the opposite: 'synthesised soft-body scenes carry no measured material behaviour'. One of the two is wrong on this corpus.
preregistered_surprise.would_change: If the agent solvers are far worse: the 76% is a same-model preference over reports and videos, the blind-judge protocol is retired as a fidelity claim, and agent-built soft-body suites are scene generators that need a validation column from GAUGE-class data before policies trained in them are reported; the lane's 'ground truth from reality' direction is confirmed with a number. If they reach parity: the audit loop produces validated-grade soft-body physics from formulas and self-run checks alone, the J06 synthesised half is usable as the suite's scene set, and the validation leg of the lane's V&V triad can be run on agent-written solvers at the same cost as on engines.

identifiability: The error $e$ is a property of (solver, scene port, parameters, GAUGE trajectory); step 1 bounds the port's contribution by reproducing a published engine number within 10% through the same scene files, and step 3 separates the agent's parameter choices from its solver form, so a reading above the engine range is attributed to the solver only after both controls pass. Contamination: GAUGE predates the card paper and the creator cites its material tables (card information_asymmetry), so step 0 reads the 25 reports for any use of GAUGE trajectories; static parameters in hand and trajectories unseen is the expected and reported condition. GAUGE's uncertainty annotations are the error bar; no LLM judges anything. The comparison is at calibrated parameters, not tuned ones, for every engine alike, matching GAUGE's protocol. Deterministic scenes; the refinement check in step 4 tells model-form error (does not shrink) from discretisation error (shrinks), which the sibling candidate measures on the task scenes.

title: Old because it is old, or old because it is true? Counterbalanced and unfamiliar-entity arms of the obsolete-fact swap
statement: Rebuild the card paper's 74 paired conflict questions from the public MemoryAgentBench FactConsolidation 6K split and rerun its equal-size swap (condition $A = \{s^{+}, u_1, u_2, u_3\}$ against $B = \{s^{-}, s^{+}, u_1, u_2\}$, where $s^{+}$ is the latest statement about the target relation, $s^{-}$ its older version and $u_j$ unrelated statements) under three value assignments at matched prompt size: original (the obsolete value is the ordinary-world fact and the latest is synthetic, as in all 50 flips of the paper's Table 17), counterbalanced (the two values swap roles, so the world fact is the latest and the synthetic value the obsolete), and unfamiliar (the subject entity is replaced by a fictional name in every statement and in the question, so neither value has a parametric anchor), with a question-only arm per assignment that reads the prior directly. Readers are the paper's Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Qwen3-14B plus Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, temperature 0, three draws of the unrelated statements per question; the outcome is the stale-selection rate $r_c$, the fraction of the 74 questions whose answer under condition $B$ matches the obsolete value, per assignment $c$. The decomposition $r_{\mathrm{orig}} = \rho + \pi_{-}$, $r_{\mathrm{unf}} = \rho$, $r_{\mathrm{cb}} = \rho - \pi_{+}$ reads $\rho$, the version-blindness rate (the reader picks the older of two in-context values when neither is backed by its weights), and $\pi_{\mp}$, the prior pull toward the world value when it is the older ($-$) or the newer ($+$) statement, off three cells the paper reports only one of.
claim: The obsolete-fact failure in agent-memory benchmarks is the reader's parametric prior winning over the context, not recency failing: when neither in-context value is a world fact the stale-selection rate falls below 15% on the same reader that shows 55%, so benchmarks that build 'updates' by replacing true facts with synthetic ones measure knowledge conflict, not memory.
trick: Swap which of the two competing values is the real-world fact, and separately make both values fictional, and see whether the reader still picks the older one.
why_now: The card paper (2610.36308, 2026-10-26) names both arms and runs neither ('establish susceptibility to these competitors, not that temporal obsolescence alone drives the effect', sec. 4), on a public split (MemoryAgentBench 2507.05257, Conflict_Resolution / FactConsolidation, released on Hugging Face) with a prompt and audit protocol specified in its App. A, so the three cells cost one afternoon of a single GPU; 2606.01435 (the paper's cited neighbour) already treats the same split as a 'freshness' task and reports 82 to 93% from pipeline separation, and 2610.41056 (2026-10-29) formalizes 'outdated memory' as a write-rule problem scored by evidence-conditioned accuracy, so the lane is building recipes on a benchmark whose stale value is always the true one.

killing_experiment.design: Step 1 (1 day, $0): download the 6K FactConsolidation history and questions, reconstruct the 74 single-older-version chains by the paper's App. A.5 chain labels, and for each question build the three assignments: original (statements as shipped), counterbalanced (exchange the object values of $s^{-}$ and $s^{+}$ while keeping their statement numbers, so the world fact now carries the higher number and is the gold), unfamiliar (replace the subject entity by a fictional name drawn from a fixed list in both statements and the question; both values kept, gold unchanged). Step 2 (1 day, about 4 GPU-hours on one 80 GB GPU via vLLM): for each assignment, each of 3 readers, conditions $A$ and $B$ and 3 draws of $u_j$ with zero content-word overlap, plus a question-only arm; about 4,400 calls of 160 to 300 prompt tokens with 64 output tokens. Score by the paper's normalized substring match against the chain values (latest / stale / unknown / other); report $r_c$ with a task-level bootstrap band over the 74 questions and the exact McNemar $p$ between original and each other assignment; report condition $A$ accuracy per assignment as the floor check (the paper's is 74/74). Optional step 3 (same cost again): render $s^{-}$ with an explicit '[superseded by #n]' tag in each assignment, the paper's own untested 'mark inactive' recommendation; its reading is a secondary readout for C-W43-09's premise (does a reader consume an explicit supersession mark) and enters no kill condition here.
killing_experiment.kills_if: On Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, $r_{\mathrm{unf}} \geq 0.40$ or $r_{\mathrm{cb}} \geq 0.40$ (within 15 points of the paper's $41/74 = 0.554$) with the bootstrap band above 0.30: the reader picks the older value without parametric help, version blindness is a reader property, the paper's temporal reading stands and the prior is a minor term. That outcome is citable as the first direct separation of recency from prior on an agent-memory benchmark and strengthens the lane's 'readers ignore version marks' sentence. Protocol kill: condition $A$ accuracy under the counterbalanced or unfamiliar assignment falls below 0.90 on the 7B reader, meaning the rewrite itself broke readability and the cells are not comparable; then the assignment is repaired before any reading.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment probability 0.6: on the 7B reader $r_{\mathrm{unf}}$ is 0.05 to 0.15 and $r_{\mathrm{cb}}$ is 0.00 to 0.05 against $r_{\mathrm{orig}}$ near 0.55, so $\pi_{-}$ is at least two thirds of the paper's 55.4-point drop; on the 14B reader $r_{\mathrm{orig}} = 0.12$ collapses to under 0.03 in both other arms; the question-only arm answers the world value in over 60% of the 74 (the paper's question-only arm scores 0/74 against synthetic gold, Table 11, which is the same fact read the other way).
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: The card paper's abstract and sec. 3.2 read the swap as evidence that 'obsolete' entries override current ones, and sec. 4 recommends that memory systems 'retire, down-weight, or explicitly mark superseded facts as inactive'; MemoryAgentBench (2507.05257) files the split under 'selective forgetting' and 2606.01435 under 'freshness'; the paper itself concedes the confound in one sentence ('In this benchmark, obsolete values often match familiar world knowledge while the synthetic updates contradict it', sec. 4) and does not stratify. The knowledge-conflict literature predicts the opposite reading: 2305.13300 reports 'a strong confirmation bias when the external evidence contains some information that is consistent with their parametric memory, despite being presented with conflicting evidence at the same time', which is the swap's condition $B$ exactly.
preregistered_surprise.would_change: If the prior is most of the drop: every memory-update benchmark built by substituting synthetic values for true ones (FactConsolidation, and any update split that edits real-world facts) owes a counterbalanced or fictional-entity stratum before a 'stale memory' number is reported, memory-system write rules motivated by these numbers (delete or tag superseded facts) are motivated by a knowledge-conflict result, and for CL-W43-05 the only reader-side override evidence in the lane does not transfer to an agent's own stale notes, which have no parametric backing, so the claim's reader cell is untested rather than occupied. If version blindness survives without the prior: the reader cannot use a statement number as a recency mark, which is the strongest reader-side support the lane has for marking or deleting superseded entries at write time, and C-W43-09's tag arm inherits a cheap prior result (step 3).
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: Either $r_{\mathrm{unf}} \leq 0.15$ on the 7B reader (prior, not recency, is the mechanism; benchmark-validity consequence) or $r_{\mathrm{unf}} \geq 0.40$ (version blindness without a prior; write-time marking consequence); the uninformative band is 0.15 to 0.40, in which the two terms are comparable and the report says so with the decomposition.

scorecard.target_value: In print: the card paper names the arm and declines it (sec. 4, quoted above); 2305.13300's confirmation-bias finding is the competing explanation stated by its own authors; MemoryAgentBench's authors (2507.05257) label the split a memory competency. Who pays: benchmark owners of update and forgetting splits (MemoryAgentBench, LongMemEval's knowledge-update category 2410.10813, MemOps 2607.12893 whose abstract names 'relying on stale values after a correction' as a failure cause), memory-system builders whose write rules cite these numbers (Stashbird 2609.34242 'corrections supersede prior active relations'; 2610.41056's outdated-memory manager), and the CL-W43-05 thread, which needs to know whether the lane's reader-side override result is about recency at all.

impact_ceiling.floor: The three cells on one benchmark and three small readers; a note that corrects the card paper's reading one way or the other; requires steps 1 and 2; probability 0.4 (judgment).
impact_ceiling.middle: The decomposition identity plus the result that the prior is most of the drop, adopted as a required stratum (counterbalanced or fictional-entity) by one memory benchmark's update split; requires step 2 and one frontier reader via API (about $20); probability 0.4 (judgment).
impact_ceiling.ceiling: The same split applied to two more update benchmarks (LongMemEval knowledge updates, MemOps update probes) shows the published stale-memory rates are mostly prior pull, changing how memory-update numbers are reported across the lane; requires two more datasets and about 20 GPU-hours; probability 0.2 (judgment).

L1 secondary: benchmark validity of update splits.

title: One wrong bullet in the agent's own summary, the right value in a fresh tool output: which one does the agent act on?
statement: Move the card paper's matched-size swap from a retrieved statement list read by a 7B model to a compaction summary read by a frontier agent in a closed loop: on AppWorld test-normal in the public SJC harness (ACON patch plus OpenClaw safeguard compressor, 4,096-token window, frozen agent; github.com/GuanghuiMin/sjc per C-W43-23's kill record), pre-select 60 tasks whose first state-changing reference call takes a literal argument (an id, email, amount or date) and whose first compaction boundary precedes that call, intercept the summary at that boundary, and insert one bullet of fixed length into its key-facts section under four matched-length contents: (U) an unrelated true fact, (S) a wrong value for that argument that an earlier environment output did contain (a sibling item from the same listing), (F) a wrong value no output ever contained, and (P) the same fabricated value written as the agent's own earlier decision ('Decided: use ... for this step'). In the main arms the harness then issues the read call that returns the current value as the first post-boundary turn, so the summary's wrong value and the environment's right value sit in the same context (the paper's condition $B$ with the summary as $s^{-}$); S and F are also run without the forced read. Score without a judge: uptake $u_c = \Pr[\text{the first post-boundary state-changing call uses the inserted value}]$ by exact normalized match, the natural re-read rate in the unforced arms, and task success, with three runs per cell.
claim: After compaction a frontier agent's own summary outranks a fresh tool output in the same context: when the two disagree on an argument the agent acts on the summary's value in more than half of runs, and no less often when no observation ever produced that value.
trick: Plant one wrong value in the agent's own compaction summary, let the environment show the right value right after, and count how often the agent acts on the summary anyway, with the planted value either something it once saw or something nothing ever produced.
why_now: The card paper (2026-10-26) shows the paired equal-size swap is a judge-free ruler for 'retrieved but overridden' and its card names the transfer to a compaction summary as the piece CL-W43-05 lacks; SJC (2610.20927, 2026-10-14) ships the harness and the compressor and reports that failed runs carry out summary entries, with no arm in which the environment contradicts the summary in view; 2606.25449 (2026-06-24) scores the same contest judge-free with an explicit correction and leaves the silent contradiction by a tool output untested; 2608.06057 (2026-08-06) shows polluted history flips 32.1% of decisions on a 1.7B model and stops at the history, not the self-written summary.

killing_experiment.design: Step 1 (about $100, 3 days): one Prompting run over 168 test-normal tasks (shared with C-W43-08 if it runs) to find tasks whose first boundary precedes the first literal-argument state-changing reference call; keep 60, pre-register the argument and its current value per task from the reference solution, the sibling value for S from the pre-boundary outputs, the fabricated value for F (same format, never printed), and one bullet wording per arm at matched token length. Step 2 (about $400, 6 days): six cells per task, U / S / F / P with the forced read and S / F without, three runs each: 1,080 continuations of 10 to 15 steps on the paper's GPT agent at its default temperature; the forced read is the reference solution's own read call, executed by the harness and appended as a normal tool turn. Compute $u_c$ per cell with a task-level bootstrap band (1,000 resamples), the paired difference $u_F - u_S$, the natural re-read rate and uptake conditional on it in the unforced arms, and success per cell; audit 50 exact-match labels by hand. Secondary: repeat S and F with forced read on MiniMax-M3 if the GPT result sits within 10 points of a kill boundary.
killing_experiment.kills_if: In the forced-read arms, $u_S$ and $u_F$ are both below 0.25 with bands under 0.35 (the fresh output displaces the summary; persistence is repaired by re-reading, so CL-W43-05's mechanism is not a reader failure for this agent and the lever is a re-read policy, which is the omission side C-W43-21 tests); or $u_F < 0.5\, u_S$ with non-overlapping bands (the agent discounts a value nothing ever produced, so provenance is partly consumed through plausibility and 'unsourced' is the less dangerous half of the summary, which contradicts the claim's noun). Protocol kill: fewer than 40 of 168 tasks meet the boundary-before-call condition, in which case the window is lowered to 2,048 tokens and the change reported, or the probe is parked if that fails too.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment probability 0.45 for the claim as written: with the forced read, $u_S$ and $u_F$ in 0.35 to 0.60 and within 10 points of each other, $u_P$ 5 to 15 points above them (the agent executes its own stated decision more readily than a stated fact), $u_U = 0$; without the forced read the natural re-read rate is under 0.4 and uptake rises to 0.6 to 0.8. Conceded in advance: a frontier agent is a stronger reader than the paper's 7B, so uptake with the right value in view can fall under 0.25, which is the first kill and is itself the lane's first number on whether re-reading repairs a self-written summary.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: SJC reads its census (29 of 35 analyzed failures follow a summary entry; 22 of 29 failure-following entries unsupported, Table 11 after the 9-run exclusion, per CL-W43-05's record) as the agent treating every summary line as established, and gates on provenance; 2607.13071 names summaries inherited 'without re-verification'; the card paper shows a 7B reader picks the stale value in 41 of 74 matched-size swaps even under an explicit recency rule (Table 16); against these, 2305.13300 reports readers 'highly receptive to external evidence' when it is coherent, and 2606.25449 finds whether a lossy memory becomes a harmful action 'is a joint model-and-interface property', which predicts the fresh output wins for a strong agent.
preregistered_surprise.would_change: If the summary outranks the fresh output regardless of provenance: re-fetching cannot repair a compaction summary, only deleting or marking at the boundary can, the claim's 'unsourced persistence' is upgraded from a failure mode to one a re-read does not fix, and every compaction evaluation owes a contradiction-in-view cell beside its length and provenance numbers. If the fresh output wins: the fix is a re-read policy after compaction (the omission side), and provenance gates (SJC, C-W43-09) address a failure the agent repairs by itself when it looks. If $u_F \ll u_S$: the agent discounts values with no plausible origin, so unsourced entries are self-limiting and the dangerous entries are stale-but-sourced ones, which reverses the claim's noun.
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: Either $u_S, u_F \geq 0.5$ with the right value in view (summary beats environment; re-read is not a fix) or $u_S, u_F \leq 0.25$ (environment beats summary; the mechanism is omission and re-read); a $u_F / u_S$ ratio under 0.5 changes the claim's noun either way.

L1 secondary: a judge-free attribution of a wrong action to the summary rather than the agent.

scorecard.density_and_ownership: Occupied: the card paper's reader-side swap on retrieved statements with small readers; SJC's harness, census and provenance gate; 2606.25449's judge-free stale-value-versus-correction scoring on induced drift, with tau-bench replication, where the correction names the error; 2608.06057's paired Original / Polluted / Oracle-State views of tool-use history on Qwen3-1.7B (history, not a self-written summary; no fresh contradicting output); 2609.02127's typed provenance guardrails (a specification with 24 conformance cases, no reader measurement); 2607.13071's case report; C-W43-09 (label vs delete on natural entries), C-W43-10 (leave-one-entry-out on natural entries), C-W43-21 (omission vs commission counts), all of which vary or count natural entries and none of which plants a controlled competitor against the environment's own value in view. Pre-window: 2302.00093 (irrelevant-context control, the U arm's precedent), 2305.13300 (confirmation bias with both values present). Kill search owed in the neighbours' words: polluted history, misleading context, stale state, re-verification, contradiction, oracle state, counter-memory, sycophancy to own output, self-consistency.
scorecard.why_now: Card paper 2026-10-26 (the ruler); SJC harness public 2026-10-14; 2606.25449 (2026-06) names the untested naturalistic case; C-W43-23's kill record (2026-10-25) established that the SJC harness is re-runnable and that 74% of AppWorld reference values are literal, which sets the task filter.
scorecard.register_and_not: Measurement: a controlled, matched-length, judge-free intervention on the agent's own summary with a recipe consequence (gate at the boundary vs re-read after it). Not a compressor, not a judge, not a memory system, not a training method, and not the card's method on a new benchmark: the carrier (a self-written summary), the competitor (the environment's live output) and the reader (a closed-loop frontier agent) all change.

identifiability: Uptake $u_c$ is random given (task, cell) only through the agent's and compressor's sampling at the provider's default temperature; AppWorld's apps are deterministic after the action, so there is no environment luck term, and the forced read returns the same current value in every run of a task. The planted bullet is a protocol choice (wording, section, length), fixed once and pre-registered; the forced read is an intervention, so the main cells are causal; the natural re-read cell is observational (an agent that re-reads is one that was unsure) and is reported as a rate, not as a cause. Exact normalized match on literal arguments is the label; composed or task-given values are excluded by the task filter and the exclusion count is reported. The 60 tasks are a filtered subset, and the headline is a property of (agent, compressor, window, task family) until a second harness agrees.
